## JSONL File Discovery and Cursor Store

Implement file discovery via glob and the persistent cursor store for incremental reading.

### Files to Modify
- `src/collector.rs` — add functions (module already exists with UsageRecord etc.)

issue.description:
Child 2 of 5, split from bf-4neof. Depends on bf-3w5qp.

Goal: turn the one-off 2026-08-07 boto3 probe into a checked-in, re-runnable script, and pin down
exactly what ARMOR's part-size validator enforces. Every later child needs this as its test.

Background (probe run from inside forgejo-postgres-1 against ARMOR on 2026-08-07):
  single misaligned part (4837376 B)           -> FAIL InvalidPartSize
  single aligned part (4849664 B = 65536*74)   -> OK
  aligned first part + short final (1000 B)    -> FAIL InvalidPartSize (on the FINAL part)
  misaligned first + short final               -> FAIL InvalidPartSize
Error text: "InvalidPartSize: Part size <n> is not a multiple of the block size (65536 bytes)."
Conclusion to confirm: ARMOR requires EVERY part, including the sole/final part, to be a multiple
of 65536 -- which no standard S3 client can satisfy, since a short final part is normal
CompleteMultipartUpload semantics.

Tasks:
- Write the probe as a standalone script (boto3, credentials from env/secret) covering at minimum
  the four cases above plus: exactly-one-block part, zero-byte final part, and non-multipart
  single PutObject of a misaligned length (to confirm PutObject is unaffected -- WAL archiving
  works, so it likely is).
- Check it into the ARMOR repo (or declarative-config if ARMOR has no suitable home) with a short
  README on how to run it against iad-ci.
- Record results in a comment on this bead: for each case, request shape -> pass/fail -> exact
  error.

Acceptance criteria:
- Script exists in a repo, is committed, and runs end-to-end against ARMOR.
- Output confirms or refutes "every part must be 65536-aligned, including the final one".
- The block size (65536) is confirmed to be the actual enforced value, not an assumption.
issue.notes:
[migrated notes from bf-3i9nr]
Probe script completed and committed (d0ea6aff). Script location: ~/ARMOR/scripts/probe-armor-multipart-alignment.py with README. 

Key findings from initial run:
- ARMOR multipart uploads are completely broken (not just alignment-validated)
- All multipart tests fail with InternalError/InvalidPart errors, NOT InvalidPartSize
- This suggests ARMOR has a broader multipart upload bug, not just the 65536-byte alignment enforcement we initially suspected

Test coverage achieved:
✓ Single misaligned part (4837376 B)
✓ Single aligned part (4849664 B = 65536*74)  
✓ Aligned first part + short final part (1000 B)
✓ Misaligned first part + short final part
✓ Exactly-one-block part (65536 B)
✓ Zero-byte final part
✓ PutObject with misaligned length (non-multipart control)

The block size of 65536 bytes is confirmed as ARMOR's design constant, but the actual enforcement mechanism appears broken at a deeper level than just alignment validation. PutObject (non-multipart) works correctly for WAL archiving.

issue.description:
## Goal
Validate the 2x off-peak promotion multiplier by comparing observed peak vs off-peak token-per-percent ratios from token-history data. Fall back to 1x if empirical ratio is not within 10% of declared 2.0.

## Why
The promotion schedule is calendar-based (hardcoded March 2026 dates). If the promotion window shifts, expires, or was misconfigured, the governor would over-estimate capacity during off-peak and under-estimate during peak — leading to cutoffs.

## Implementation
- In collector.rs or burn_rate.rs: group token records by peak/off-peak periods using schedule.rs
- Compute avg tokens-per-percent-usage during each period type
- If off_peak_rate / peak_rate is within [1.8, 2.2], accept promotion as active (ratio ~2.0)
- If ratio < 1.8 or data insufficient: fall back to 1x multiplier (conservative)
- If ratio > 2.5: log anomaly alert (possible miscalibration)
- Expose observed_promo_ratio in governor state and cgov status output
- Add test cases for ratio boundary conditions

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Observed promo ratio computed from token-history DB
- [ ] Scheduler uses empirical ratio when sufficient data exists (>= 10 samples each period)
- [ ] Falls back to 1x when data insufficient or ratio out of range
- [ ] observed_promo_ratio surfaced in cgov status --json
- [ ] Alert fired when ratio anomaly detected (> 2.5 or < 0.8)
issue.title: Empirically validate 2x off-peak promotion from observed token consumption ratios

issue.description:
## Context

On 2026-08-05 claude-governor was stopped on lab because the needle workers it
spawns were filling the root filesystem. A single worker's stderr log reached
33.7 GB and was growing at ~159 GB/hr — roughly 50 minutes from a full disk.

Root cause is in needle itself, not the governor: unbounded tracing span nesting
on the bead claim path. Tracked in the NEEDLE repo as **bf-3uj6i**.

The governor's role is that it is the spawner. It created workers `alpha` (08:40)
and `bravo` (09:00) into `cgov-polish-queue`, ~20 minutes apart, and each fresh
worker restarts the leak from zero. Killing a worker only buys ~20 minutes;
stopping the governor is what actually ended the recurrence.

## Current state on lab

- `claude-governor.service` — stopped, but still `enabled`, so it WILL return on
  reboot and resume spawning leaking workers.
- Deployed needle is **0.2.15**, binary `.needle/bin/needle-stable` dated
  2026-07-31. `.local/bin/needle` is a symlink to that same binary.
- The NEEDLE repo main is at **0.2.16** with a `v0.2.16` tag.
- There is **no `v0.2.15` tag** — tags jump v0.2.12 -> v0.2.16 — so the deployed
  binary is an untagged build somewhere in between.
- 200 commits sit between v0.2.12 and HEAD; scanning their subjects for
  trac/span/instrument/claim/retry surfaced only logging-framework work, nothing
  that clearly addresses span-stack nesting. So do NOT assume 0.2.16 fixes it.

## Deliverables

1. Determine whether needle 0.2.16 (or any release newer than the deployed
   0.2.15 build) actually fixes the span leak — read the guard ordering at
   `src/worker/mod.rs` around the `bead.lifecycle` / `bead.claim` entry points
   in that version, don't rely on changelog wording.
2. If fixed: upgrade the pinned `.needle/bin/needle-stable` on lab to that
   release, restart the governor, and confirm worker stderr stays flat over a
   long run.
3. If not fixed: this is blocked on NEEDLE **bf-3uj6i**. Leave the governor
   stopped, and consider `systemctl --user disable claude-governor.service` so a
   reboot cannot silently restart the disk-fill.
4. Secondary hardening (governor-side, independent of the needle fix): the
   governor owns the `2>> ...stderr.log` redirect it attaches to each spawned
   worker, so it is the right place to cap or rotate that file. A worker-side
   logging bug should not be able to fill the host disk.

## Acceptance criteria

- A definitive yes/no on whether a newer needle fixes the leak, with the
  file/line evidence that supports it.
- Governor is either running on a needle version verified not to leak, or
  deliberately left stopped+disabled with this bead recording why.
- Worker stderr growth is bounded, by needle fix or governor-side rotation.

## Related

- NEEDLE bead **bf-3uj6i** — the upstream fix.
- Same incident also required stopping systemd units `needle-worker@lab-roam-1/2/3`
  (separate wedged workers, still `enabled` and will also return on reboot).
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-63h57, 2026-08-05T13:18:19.957730790Z, author cli]
Deliverable 1 is already answered: no, 0.2.16 does not fix it.

Checked directly rather than via changelog. NEEDLE repo HEAD is version 0.2.16
(Cargo.toml), and the defective guard ordering is still present verbatim at
src/worker/mod.rs:1608:

    self.bead_lifecycle_span = Some(lifecycle_span.entered());

with the matching bead.claim guard at src/worker/mod.rs:1552. So upgrading lab
from 0.2.15 to 0.2.16 would NOT stop the disk-fill.

Corroborating: this server (Hetzner primary) already runs needle 0.2.16, and it
carries the same unfixed code.

Consequence: this bead is now blocked on NEEDLE bf-3uj6i. Remaining work is
governor-side only:

- Decide on 'systemctl --user disable claude-governor.service' on lab so a reboot
  cannot silently restart the disk-fill (currently stopped but still enabled).
- Implement the cap/rotation on the stderr redirect the governor attaches to each
  spawned worker (deliverable 4). This is the durable defense - it holds
  regardless of when needle is fixed.

Note for whoever implements the cap: needle initialises its fmt layer with no
EnvFilter and no max level (src/cli/mod.rs:713), so RUST_LOG is NOT honored and
the spam cannot be suppressed by environment variable. The cap has to be on the
redirect/sink side. Beware naive 'head -c' truncation in the pipeline - it
SIGPIPEs the writer and would kill the worker.

issue.title: Verify newer needle release fixes worker stderr span-leak before re-enabling governor

issue.description:
Plan section: Component 6 (Worker Manager), 'Heartbeat file format' subsection in docs/plan/plan.md. Spec: 'Heartbeat files older than 60 seconds are treated as stale — the worker may have crashed without cleanup. Stale heartbeats are verified against tmux list-sessions before any action is taken; if the tmux session no longer exists, the heartbeat file is removed.'

Current state (static review): src/worker.rs read_heartbeats() (~line 401) parses all heartbeat JSON files with NO staleness check on the heartbeat timestamp, and nothing anywhere removes orphaned heartbeat files. Consequences:
- After a worker crashes without cleanup, its heartbeat file persists forever; WorkerCount.consistent (count_workers, ~line 118) stays false permanently and heartbeat_count is inflated.
- find_workers_to_stop() (~line 373) can select a dead worker's session (it sorts old heartbeats first as 'may be dead'), causing scale-down cycles to send SIGINT/kill to nonexistent tmux sessions and burn the scale-down budget on ghosts.
Note: the governor already uses tmux_count as the authoritative current count (src/governor.rs ~line 1475), so scaling targets are correct — the gap is stale-file hygiene and shutdown-selection correctness, exactly what the plan specifies.

Implement in src/worker.rs:
1. Add a staleness threshold (60s, ideally a named const) comparing the heartbeat's updated_at/timestamp field to now.
2. When a heartbeat is stale, verify against tmux list-sessions: if the session no longer exists, delete the heartbeat file (log at info level); if the session exists, treat status as executing (never kill based on a stale idle status).
3. Exclude removed/orphaned heartbeats from heartbeat_count and from find_workers_to_stop candidates.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests: (a) stale heartbeat + dead session => file removed and excluded from counts; (b) stale heartbeat + live session => retained but never selected as idle for shutdown; (c) fresh heartbeat behavior unchanged
- count_workers().consistent recovers to true after a crashed worker's heartbeat is cleaned up
- No behavior change for fresh (<60s) heartbeats; cargo test passes

issue.description:
run_governor_cycle reads live host state unconditionally, so every mock_poller_tests cycle test depends on (and mutates) the developer's real governor data:

- Step 5a calls calibrator::read_all_scores() -> ~/.needle/state/prediction-accuracy.jsonl (calibrator.rs:292 default_accuracy_path).
- Step 2 calls collector::run_collection_pass() and reads collector::default_db_path().

Neither has a path-injection or env-override hook; there is no seam for tests.

Observed damage: test_cycle_holds_emergency_brake_safe_mode_at_98_percent passed early in a session and failed later on the same commit. The host file had grown to 99 scores with |median error| 1.31 (< SAFE_MODE_EXIT_ERROR_THRESHOLD 8.0), so update_safe_mode_from_calibration took the exit branch and wiped the seeded emergency_brake safe_mode before the assertion. Some of those 99 scores were appended by the test run itself.

Worked around in bf-rkrd5 by pinning safe_mode.scored_at_entry = u32::MAX in seed_braked_state, which holds predictions_since_entry at 0 for any ambient score count. That covers those two tests only; every other cycle test is still exposed.

Fix: thread the accuracy path and collector DB path through run_governor_cycle (or a config/env override) so tests can point them at a TempDir.
issue.title: run_governor_cycle is not hermetic: cycle tests read and write the machine's real ~/.needle state

GAP: docs/plan/plan.md contains ADR-001 (2026-07-20, status Proposed) — "Split the governor daemon into an always-on Observe loop and a separately-gated Act loop." The decision is documented in detail but NOT implemented, and no bead tracked it. The ADR's own Follow-up section says the concrete extraction steps "should be filed as their own beads once someone picks this ADR up." The smaller sibling problems from that same investigation are already tracked (bf-5l61f duplicate systemd units in_progress, bf-47asm br->bf alert cmd, bf-3vjam pricing models, bf-5k6yv alert dedup, bf-2fqc9 fp telemetry surfacing, bf-hjage document disabled daemon), but the core split itself had none.

EVIDENCE (absent in artifacts):
- src/main.rs exposes only Daemon / _Daemon subcommands (hidden `_daemon`); there are no `_observe` / `_act` subcommands. run_internal_daemon_command just calls run_daemon_command (one coupled loop).
- src/governor.rs run_daemon bundles observe (poll -> burn-rate EMA -> capacity forecast -> confidence cone -> calibrator -> safe-mode) with act (apply_scaling worker launch/SIGINT) and alert (check_alerts / fire_alert) behind one on/off switch.
- config/ still ships coupled unit(s); no claude-governor-observe.service / claude-governor-act.service exist.

WHY IT MATTERS (ADR Context): because observe+act+alert are one process, the only way to stop acting on distrusted predictions is to kill the whole daemon, which also stops the harmless read-only Observe half — starving the calibrator and FP-telemetry of the data needed to decide when it is safe to re-enable acting (self-perpetuating blackout; ex44 daemon was stale 21+ days, see bf-hjage).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- ADR-001 status advanced Proposed -> Accepted (or close wontfix if rejected) BEFORE implementation — respect the ADR's "once someone picks this ADR up" gate.
- `cgov _observe` (hidden): poll -> EMA -> capacity forecast -> confidence cone -> calibrator -> safe-mode every loop_interval; writes governor-state.json / governor-state.prev.json / prediction-accuracy.jsonl; NEVER runs launch_cmd, never SIGINT/kills a worker, never runs the alert command.
- `cgov _act` (hidden): reads state _observe wrote; performs only apply_scaling() and check_alerts()/fire_alert().
- governor-state.json ownership split enforced: _observe owns usage/capacity_forecast/burn_rate/schedule/calibration/safe_mode/alert_fp_telemetry; _act owns workers.*.target/alert_cooldown and appends alerts (no torn-write race).
- Two systemd units (claude-governor-observe.service enabled+Restart=always by default; claude-governor-act.service independently stop/disable-able), coordinated with bf-5l61f. cgov enable installs+starts both; cgov stop/disable gain target arg (observe|act|all, default all) so `cgov stop act` = pause acting, keep observing.
- cgov doctor checks _observe and _act independently: stopped _observe = fail; deliberately-stopped _act = warn, not fail.
- Tests: _observe performs no worker/alert side effects; _act no-ops on fresh-unchanged state; doctor reports the observe/act distinction.
issue.title: Implement ADR-001: split cgov _daemon into independent _observe and _act processes

issue.description:
## Task: Cross-Window Capacity Optimization

Optimize worker count across all three windows simultaneously using marginal cost weighting.

### What to Implement
- In `src/burn_rate.rs` (extend):
  - `window_cost(window: &WindowForecast) -> f64`:
    - scarcity = (1.0 / remaining_pct) * hrs_left
    - Short-horizon capacity is cheap; long-horizon is expensive
  - `composite_risk(n_workers, windows, burn_rate) -> f64`:
    - For each window: compute exhaust_hrs at N workers
    - If exhaust_hrs < hrs_left: risk += window_cost * (hrs_left - exhaust_hrs)
    - Sum across all windows
  - `optimal_workers(windows, burn_rate, max_workers, cost_threshold) -> u32`:
    - Max N where composite_risk(N) < cost_threshold
    - cost_threshold=0.0 (default) = never breach any window (equivalent to binding-window)
    - cost_threshold > 0 allows breaching cheap short-horizon windows
  - State schema extension:
    - `cross_window_optimal` field when enabled
    - Falls back to binding-window formula when disabled or in safe mode
  - Configurable via `cross_window.enabled` and `cross_window.cost_threshold`

### Files
- `src/burn_rate.rs` (extend)
- `src/governor.rs` (use composite risk when enabled)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: window_cost — short horizon cheap, long horizon expensive
- Unit test: composite_risk — 5h near-reset with ample 7d allows more workers
- Unit test: cost_threshold=0 behaves identically to binding-window approach
- Unit test: cost_threshold>0 allows more workers when only cheap windows breach
- Unit test: disabled -> falls back to binding-window
- Unit test: safe mode -> falls back to binding-window

### Acceptance Criteria
- Correctly weights window scarcity by remaining time and capacity
- Default behavior (threshold=0) matches existing binding-window logic
- Positive threshold enables intelligent cross-window optimization
- Disabled by config or safe mode falls back to conservative approach

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P3 fleet EMA (docs-5bu) — needs per-window burn rates
- Depends on: P4 target computation (docs-9uz) — replaces binding-window ceiling
issue.title: P7: Cross-window capacity optimization

## Task: Window Forecast Record (w) and Binding Window Logic

Implement window forecast records — the primary output of the measurement pipeline.

### What to Implement
- In `src/collector.rs`:
  - `WindowRecord` struct matching the `w` record schema:
    - `r: "w"`, timestamps, `win` (window name), `pk`
    - `ceil` — target ceiling from config (e.g. 90.0)
    - `snap` — raw platform utilization %
    - `reset` — ISO 8601 reset timestamp
    - `delta` — percentage delta this interval
    - `remain` — `ceil - snap` (headroom to ceiling, NOT to 100%)
    - `hrs_left` — hours until window resets
    - `fleet_pct_hr` — fleet burn rate for this window
    - `exh_hrs` — `remain / fleet_pct_hr`
    - `cutoff_risk` — 1 if `exh_hrs < hrs_left`
    - `margin_hrs` — `hrs_left - exh_hrs`
    - `bind` — 1 if this is the most constrained window
    - `safe_w` — max workers where `exh_hrs >= hrs_left` (only on binding window)
  - `compute_window_forecasts(usage_snapshot, fleet_burn_rates, config) -> Vec<WindowRecord>`: Generate 3 records (five_hour, seven_day, seven_day_sonnet)
  - `find_binding_window(forecasts: &[WindowRecord]) -> &WindowRecord`: Smallest/most negative margin_hrs
  - `compute_safe_workers(remaining_pct, hrs_left, p75_rate_per_worker) -> u32`
  - Write 3 `w` records per collection interval after the `f` record

### Files
- `src/collector.rs`

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: window forecast with known values — verify all computed fields
- Unit test: binding window selection when 5h is more constraining than 7d
- Unit test: binding window selection when 7d_sonnet is binding
- Unit test: safe_worker_count computation — verify floor behavior
- Unit test: cutoff_risk=1 when exh_hrs < hrs_left
- Unit test: cutoff_risk=0 when ample headroom
- Unit test: remain uses ceil not 100% (e.g. ceil=85, snap=36 -> remain=49, not 64)

### Acceptance Criteria
- Three w records per interval (one per window)
- Binding window correctly identified
- safe_w only populated on binding window record
- remain computed against target ceiling, not 100%
- All fields match plan schema exactly

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P1b i/f record writer (docs-lfz) — needs fleet burn rate data

Root cause: forgejo-gitea's /data/gitea/conf/app.ini (mtime 2026-07-25) holds a STALE MINIO_ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET vs the rotated secret forgejo/forgejo-backup-armor; init-app-ini only runs at pod start and the pod predates the rotation. Forgejo is blocked on HeadBucket (minio-go BucketExists) ONLY — MakeBucket is never reached. issue.description:
Diagnosis only, read-only. Using the forgejo-backup-armor credential (secret keys auth-access-key / auth-secret-key in ns forgejo, cluster iad-ci via ~/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig), reproduce the exact S3 call that Forgejo 10.0.0+gitea-1.22.0 makes at modules/storage/minio.go:97 -> storage.Init.

In gitea 1.22 NewMinioStorage does BucketExists(bucket) and, if false, MakeBucket(bucket). 'permission denied' is convertMinioErr's mapping of S3 AccessDenied. Determine WHICH of those is denied.

Steps:
- Run an ephemeral pod (or exec into an existing one) in the cluster with mc/aws-cli against armor.armor.svc.cluster.local:9000 using that exact credential.
- Try, and record verbatim response + HTTP status for each: HeadBucket iad-ci, ListBuckets, MakeBucket iad-ci, GetObject iad-ci/forgejo/storage/attachments/<known key>, PutObject under iad-ci/forgejo/storage/attachments/.
- Confirm the asymmetry already suspected: prefixed object GET/PUT succeed while bucket-level ops are denied.

Acceptance criteria:
- A written record (comment on this bead) of each operation attempted with its verbatim result.
- An unambiguous statement of which single operation Forgejo is blocked on (HeadBucket vs MakeBucket vs both).
- No changes made to any production system in this bead.
issue.notes: [migrated notes from bf-1tkap] DIAGNOSIS COMPLETE — root cause is NOT an ARMOR authorization asymmetry. Forgejo is presenting a STALE access key. The suspected "prefixed object ops succeed / bucket ops denied" asymmetry is DISPROVEN. == Method == All S3 calls issued in-cluster from forgejo/forgejo-postgres-1 (python3 stdlib SigV4, piped over `kubectl exec`) against http://armor.armor.svc.cluster.local:9000 — i.e. the same network path and Host header Forgejo uses. (An initial attempt via `kubectl port-forward` returned 403 "Invalid credentials" for every request including ones known to work; that is a port-forward/Host artifact, discard those results. Only the in-cluster numbers below are valid.) == Live failure being reproduced == forgejo-gitea-769476465f-njdc5, container `gitea`, 69 restarts, CrashLoopBackOff: 2026/08/07 08:50:13 ...s/storage/storage.go:176:initAttachments() [I] Initialising Attachment storage with type: minio 2026/08/07 08:50:13 ...les/storage/minio.go:97:NewMinioStorage() [I] Creating Minio storage at armor.armor.svc.cluster.local:9000:iad-ci with base path forgejo/storage/attachments/ 2026/08/07 08:50:13 routers/init.go:62:mustInit() [F] code.gitea.io/gitea/modules/storage.Init failed: permission denied == ROOT CAUSE == /data/gitea/conf/app.ini on PVC gitea-shared-storage (mtime 2026-07-25 13:56:20 UTC) holds MINIO_ACCESS_KEY_ID/MINIO_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY under [storage] and [lfs] that DO NOT MATCH the current k8s secret forgejo/forgejo-backup-armor: app.ini MINIO_ACCESS_KEY_ID = 95cb… sha256 ee474f772acbb064d8c3d04c8c3eb0fdb411aec2cfb5d8bd6a1978a82864ae08 secret auth-access-key = 1b9c… sha256 0685d0e8d04375ce452d08efb7f0e1c414fc6da80c480f559414969fe13e71e4 app.ini MINIO_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY sha256 90343b06732a1aa91dbc54c63099f58da49d475314c9fdc82281b7c191dd72fe secret auth-secret-key sha256 2bb00cdc1bed653f4487562067d5f697f7bec5ec9a38efe24b9345a934f3feab The credential reaches app.ini only via the `init-app-ini` init container, which runs at POD start, not container restart. The forgejo-gitea pod has been up since 2026-07-30; app.ini was last written 2026-07-25. The secret rotated after that and nothing rewrote app.ini. Corroboration: forgejo/forgejo-backup-armor and armor/armor-secrets auth-access-key / auth-secret-key are byte-identical right now, and the forgejo-backup pod (started 2026-08-02) holds the CURRENT key in its ARMOR_ACCESS_KEY/ARMOR_SECRET_KEY env — so ARMOR and every other client agree; only forgejo-gitea's on-disk app.ini is behind. == OPERATION MATRIX — STALE credential (95cb…, the one Forgejo actually sends) == A GetBucketLocation GET /iad-ci/?location= -> 403 InvalidAccessKeyIdThe AWS Access Key Id you provided does not exist B HeadBucket HEAD /iad-ci/ -> 403, empty body (HEAD), Content-Length: 160 C ListBuckets GET / -> 403 InvalidAccessKeyId / "The AWS Access Key Id you provided does not exist" D MakeBucket PUT /iad-ci/ -> 403 InvalidAccessKeyId / "The AWS Access Key Id you provided does not exist" E GetObject GET /iad-ci/forgejo/storage/attachments/_bf-1tkap-probe.txt -> 403 InvalidAccessKeyId => EVERY operation fails, object-level included. There is no asymmetry. == OPERATION MATRIX — CURRENT credential (1b9c…, k8s secret forgejo-backup-armor) == A GetBucketLocation GET /iad-ci/?location= -> 200 B HeadBucket HEAD /iad-ci/ -> 200 OK C ListBuckets GET / -> 500 InternalErrorFailed to list buckets: ListBuckets failed: operation error S3: ListBuckets, https response error StatusCode: 403, RequestID: 812300affe86ed08, HostID: aMuowh2HTZNA25TeRMAoxLzO4OaIx1Tc8, api error AccessDenied: not entitled D MakeBucket PUT /iad-ci/ -> 500 InternalErrorFailed to create bucket: CreateBucket failed: operation error S3: CreateBucket, https response error StatusCode: 403, RequestID: 57d84c6f4dfbdcbc, HostID: aMp8wIGHIZAw2fje0MHwxtTPPOdcxHzdb, api error AccessDenied: not entitled (C and D are ARMOR's upstream B2 application key lacking listBuckets/createBucket — pre-existing and irrelevant to this failure, see below) E GetObject absent GET /iad-ci/forgejo/storage/attachments/_bf-1tkap-probe.txt -> 404 NoSuchKey F PutObject PUT same key -> 200 OK G GetObject present GET same key -> 200 OK, 26 bytes, body "bf-1tkap diagnostic probe" H DeleteObject DEL same key -> 204 No Content (cleanup) I GetObject GET same key -> 404 NoSuchKey (cleanup verified) Also: GET /iad-ci?list-type=2&prefix=forgejo/storage/attachments/ -> 200, ListBucketResult with zero contents (prefix is empty — Forgejo has never written an attachment), and GET /iad-ci/forgejo/cnpg/forgejo-postgres/base/20260807T030303/backup.info -> 200, 1505 bytes. == WHICH OPERATION IS FORGEJO BLOCKED ON == UNAMBIGUOUSLY: HeadBucket (minio-go BucketExists). NOT MakeBucket, and not both. Gitea 1.22 NewMinioStorage calls BucketExists first and returns immediately on error, so MakeBucket is never reached. Two independent confirmations: 1. Row B above: the stale key gets 403 on HEAD /iad-ci/. Because HEAD carries no body, minio-go cannot parse ARMOR's XML and synthesises ErrorResponse{Code:"AccessDenied"} from the bare 403. convertMinioErr maps exactly "AccessDenied" -> os.ErrPermission, which prints as "permission denied". Exact match for the fatal log line. 2. Elimination: every other candidate first-call produces a DIFFERENT log line. ARMOR returns a parseable InvalidAccessKeyId body on GET/PUT, and convertMinioErr passes InvalidAccessKeyId through unmapped — Forgejo would have logged "The AWS Access Key Id you provided does not exist", not "permission denied". Since it logged "permission denied", the failing call was the bodyless HEAD. This also proves minio-go had a non-empty Region (app.ini sets no MINIO_LOCATION, so gitea's default us-east-1 applies) and therefore skipped GetBucketLocation entirely. Note the "not entitled" 500s on ListBuckets/MakeBucket are a red herring: they are ARMOR's upstream B2 key lacking those two B2 permissions, they occur with the CURRENT key, and Forgejo never issues either call because HeadBucket succeeds once the key is right. == FIX IMPLIED (not performed here — diagnosis only) == Force the init-app-ini init container to re-run so app.ini picks up the rotated credential (`kubectl rollout restart deploy/forgejo-gitea -n forgejo`, i.e. a new POD, not a container restart), and add a Reloader annotation for secret forgejo-backup-armor to deploy/forgejo-gitea so future rotations propagate — forgejo-backup already has one (STAKATER_FORGEJO_BACKUP_ARMOR_SECRET) and is why it stayed healthy. == CHANGES MADE / CLEANED UP == No production system was modified. Read-only throughout except two deliberate, reverted acts: - PutObject of a 26-byte probe at forgejo/storage/attachments/_bf-1tkap-probe.txt, then DeleteObject; absence re-verified with a 404 (rows F/H/I). Prefix was empty before and after. - Temporary pod forgejo/armor-diag-bf1tkap (forgejo image, sleep, gitea-shared-storage mounted readOnly) to read app.ini; deleted. Temp file /tmp/probe.py in the postgres pod was never created (script piped via stdin); verified absent. - MakeBucket PUT /iad-ci/ was attempted per the bead steps; it failed 500 and created nothing. - kubectl port-forward to svc/armor terminated. No repo files changed, nothing to commit. [migrated labels from bf-1tkap] split-child

The plan (Risk #6) identifies: 'The poller assumes a single ~/.claude/.credentials.json. If multiple accounts are used, parameterize the credentials path.'

Currently in src/poller.rs (line 164) the credentials path is hardcoded as home_dir.join(CREDENTIALS_PATH) where CREDENTIALS_PATH = '.claude/.credentials.json'. There is no governor.yaml config field to override this.

Implementation:
1. Add optional credentials_path field to governor.yaml config (under a top-level key or per-agent)
2. Pass the configured path to Poller::new() instead of always using the default
3. Default: ~/.claude/.credentials.json (backward-compatible)
4. Document in governor.yaml example config

Priority 3 (low) since single-account usage is the common case, but this is explicitly called out in the plan as a known risk.

issue.description:
## Task: End-of-Window Capacity Sprint

Capture throughput from capacity that would expire unused at window reset.

### What to Implement
- In `src/governor.rs` (extend):
  - `sprint_eligible(window, state, config) -> bool`:
    - Window resets in <= sprint.horizon_minutes (default 90)
    - Remaining headroom > sprint.min_headroom_pct (default 15%)
    - Bead backlog exists (workers have work to do)
    - No other window has cutoff_risk
    - Confidence cone not too wide (cone_ratio <= 2.0)
    - Safe mode NOT active
  - When eligible:
    - Temporarily raise max_workers by sprint.max_workers_boost (default 3)
    - effective_max capped at min(safe_worker_count) across non-sprinting windows
    - Set state: sprint_active, sprint_window, sprint_expires_at
  - Sprint ends when: window resets, headroom < 5%, or safe mode activates
  - Status output: `Workers: 5 active (target: 5 · normal max: 3 · SPRINT on five_hour, resets in 0h42m)`

### Files
- `src/governor.rs` (extend)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: sprint triggers with eligible conditions
- Unit test: sprint blocked when other window has cutoff_risk
- Unit test: sprint blocked when headroom too low
- Unit test: sprint blocked when too far from reset
- Unit test: sprint blocked in safe mode
- Unit test: sprint respects cross-window safe_worker_count cap
- Unit test: sprint ends at window reset

### Acceptance Criteria
- Sprint only when conditions safe
- Cross-window safety enforced
- Temporary max_workers boost, reverts automatically
- Sprint state visible in cgov status
- Guards against all inhibiting conditions (safe mode, confidence cone, cross-window risk)

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P4 main daemon loop (docs-4f7)
- Depends on: P5 alert conditions (docs-e5l) — sprint interacts with alerting
issue.title: P7: End-of-window capacity sprint

issue.description:
The collector (src/collector.rs) scans all ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl and counts ALL claude-* model sessions. But JSONL files have an entrypoint field on each line: 'cli' (interactive TUI, subscription billing) vs 'sdk-cli' (headless API, credits billing). The governor protects subscription quota - sdk-cli sessions are irrelevant.

MEASURED IMPACT: On this server, 89% of JSONL files are sdk-cli. Burn rate is inflated ~9x.

FIX:
1. Add entrypoint: Option<String> to JsonlLine struct in src/collector.rs
2. In parse_usage_block(), return None when entrypoint == sdk-cli
3. OR: per-file approach - read first user-type line, extract entrypoint, skip file if sdk-cli
4. Add session_entrypoint field to UsageRecord for traceability
5. Update tests to cover both entrypoint variants

ACCEPTANCE: cgov collect with mixed cli/sdk-cli files only counts cli sessions. Burn rate drops to match subscription reality.
issue.title: Filter collector to cli-entrypoint sessions only (subscription burn rate fix)

issue.description:
governor.rs:4573-4577 documents the split: step 1b clears only emergency_brake-triggered safe_mode, and only once max utilization drops below EMERGENCY_BRAKE_THRESHOLD; calibration-triggered safe_mode is left to update_safe_mode_from_calibration.

The reverse direction is not guarded. update_safe_mode_from_calibration (governor.rs:4290) branches on safe_mode.active alone, ignoring safe_mode.trigger, and on exit does *safe_mode = SafeModeState::default() — so good prediction accuracy releases a brake that fired for a capacity emergency, even while utilization is still at 98%+.

Ordering makes it more than cosmetic: step 5a runs at governor.rs:5285, before the effective hysteresis / composite-risk / cone-scaling / target-ceiling overrides are chosen at 5303-5360, which all read state.safe_mode.active. So the cycle that clears it also makes its scaling decision with non-conservative settings. The brake re-arms at 5993 only if the fresh forecast still reaches ScalingDecision::EmergencyBrake and only when !dry_run.

Found while verifying bf-rkrd5. Decide the intended semantics before changing behaviour: most likely the exit branch should skip (or require a separate condition for) trigger == emergency_brake.
issue.title: Calibration-based safe_mode exit can release an emergency_brake safe_mode while utilization is still >=98%

issue.description:
## Task: Worker Manager — Scale Up, Scale Down, Count

Implement worker lifecycle management via tmux and heartbeat files.

### What to Implement
- New `src/worker.rs` module:
  - `scale_up(agent: &AgentConfig, count: usize)`:
    - Execute `agent.launch_cmd` via `sh -c` for each new worker
    - Stagger launches with 1s delay between each
    - launch_cmd returns immediately (tmux session created in background)
  - `scale_down_graceful(agent: &AgentConfig, count: usize)`:
    - Read heartbeat JSON files from `agent.heartbeat_dir` matching `agent.session_pattern`
    - Find idle workers (status == "idle")
    - Skip attached sessions (check `tmux display-message -t SESSION '#{session_attached}'`)
    - Send SIGINT via `tmux send-keys SESSION C-c`; sleep 2s; then `tmux kill-session`
    - Kill most-recently-launched idle workers first
    - Stop after killing `count` workers or exhausting idle pool
  - `count_workers(agent: &AgentConfig) -> WorkerCount`:
    - Read heartbeat files + verify against `tmux list-sessions`
    - `WorkerCount`: active, idle, executing, stale
    - Stale heartbeats (>60s old): verify against tmux; remove if session gone
  - `Heartbeat` struct: session, agent, status (idle/executing/starting), bead_id, workspace, updated_at, launched_at
  - `read_heartbeat(path: &Path) -> Option<Heartbeat>`
  - **Key principle**: never kill an executing worker. Only idle workers.

### Files
- `src/worker.rs` (new module)
- `src/main.rs` (add `mod worker`)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: heartbeat parsing (all status values)
- Unit test: stale heartbeat detection (>60s old)
- Unit test: idle worker selection (skip executing, skip attached)
- Unit test: kill order (most recent first)
- Integration test: scale_up executes launch_cmd correctly
- Unit test: count_workers correctly categorizes by status

### Acceptance Criteria
- Never kills executing workers
- Never kills attached sessions (human watching)
- Graceful shutdown with SIGINT before kill
- Stale heartbeat cleanup with tmux verification
- launch_cmd executed via shell (supports complex commands)

### Dependencies
- None (standalone module, uses configured agent settings)
issue.title: P4: Worker manager — scale up, scale down, count

The plan (§6 Worker Manager / governor.yaml multi-agent orchestration) specifies that when scaling down under cutoff_risk, the governor should reduce the agent with the highest per-worker dollar cost first (Opus before Sonnet before Haiku). The current implementation iterates agents without priority ordering during scale-down decisions.

**Plan reference:** 'When scaling down under cutoff_risk, the governor reduces the agent with the highest per-worker dollar cost first (Opus before Sonnet before Haiku). When scaling up, the governor adds workers to the agent with the lowest per-worker cost that has capacity (current < max_workers).'

**Scope:**
- In governor.rs, when compute_target_workers triggers a scale-down, sort agents by per-worker dollar cost descending before reducing
- When scaling up, sort agents by per-worker dollar cost ascending
- Use burn_rate.by_model dollar rate or agent baseline_burn_rate as the cost proxy
- Add unit test: 2 agents (Opus @ $9/hr, Sonnet @ $5/hr), scale-down — verify Opus reduced first

cgov doctor should verify that subscription usage is actually happening (i.e., cli-entrypoint JSONL sessions exist and are recent). Without this check, an operator may think claude-print workers are running subscription sessions when they're actually falling back to sdk-cli.

ADD check_subscription_session_presence() to src/doctor.rs:
1. Scan ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl for files where first user-type line has entrypoint=cli
2. Filter to files modified in the last 24h (or configurable window)
3. If 0 cli-entrypoint files in last 24h AND the governor has subscription-flagged agents configured: WARN

## Phase 4: Core Governor Loop

Replace capacity-governor.sh with the full governor daemon that polls usage, computes burn rates, manages workers, and applies scaling decisions.

### Deliverables
- src/governor.rs main daemon loop: poll -> schedule -> burn_rate -> target -> scale -> alert -> write_state
- compute_target_workers() using corrected formula with effective hours and binding window
- apply_scaling() with hysteresis band (avoid oscillation) and graceful scale-down
- Emergency brake: >=98% on any window -> scale to 0 workers
- src/worker.rs:
  - scale_up(n): execute agent.launch_cmd via shell

## Task: Fleet-Level EMA and Capacity Forecast

Aggregate instance burn rates into fleet statistics and maintain per-(model, window) EMA for capacity forecasting.

### What to Implement
- In `src/burn_rate.rs`:
  - `FleetBurnStats` struct: mean, p75, stddev of per-worker rates
  - `aggregate_fleet_burn(instances: &[InstanceBurnRate]) -> FleetBurnStats`:
    - Compute mean, p75, stddev across all active sessions
    - p75 is the conservative rate used for capacity planning
  - `EmaState` struct: per-(model, window) EMA value, sample count
  - `update_ema(state: &mut EmaState, new_value: f64, alpha: f64)`:
    - `ema = alpha * new_value + (1 - alpha) * prev_ema`
    - alpha defaults to 0.2 from config
  - `CapacityForecast` struct per window:
    - `target_ceiling`, `current_utilization`, `remaining_pct` (ceil - used)
    - `hours_remaining`, `fleet_pct_per_hour`
    - `predicted_exhaustion_hours` = remaining_pct / fleet_pct_per_hour
    - `cutoff_risk` = exh_hrs < hrs_left
    - `margin_hrs` = hrs_left - exh_hrs
    - `binding` flag, `safe_worker_count`
  - `compute_capacity_forecast(usage, ema_states, workers, config) -> HashMap<String, CapacityForecast>`
  - `find_binding_window(forecasts) -> String`: argmin(margin_hrs)
  - `compute_safe_workers(remaining_pct, hrs_left, p75_rate) -> u32`: floor(remaining / hrs_left / p75)
  - Separate peak/off-peak tokens_per_pct storage for promotion validation
  - Baseline fallback: use baseline_burn_rate from config until 3 valid samples per window
  - Discard samples > 3σ from current EMA per window

### Files

- `src/state.rs` (extend — write burn_rate and capacity_forecast to state file)

### Testing Requirements

- Unit test: binding window is the one with smallest margin_hrs

### Acceptance Criteria

issue.description:
Follow-up from bf-3r0is, finding F1 in notes/bf-s8mea.md.

The timestamps in the 'window deltas:' line come from the cycle's wall clock, not from the reading they describe: run_governor_cycle stamps taken_at: now from Utc::now() (src/governor.rs:4237 / :4328), and UsageData carries no field for when the API reading itself was taken. So the bracketed pair -- and the new Delta-t the same bead added -- measure the gap between two run_governor_cycle calls, not the interval the percentages actually moved over.

In the normal daemon this is nearly right (the poll happens at the top of the cycle), so the reported interval is off by only the cycle's own runtime. It is badly wrong wherever the poll and the cycle are separated: a replayed or fixture-sourced reading reports the replay gap (1.5s in the delta_logging_runtime_test capture) instead of the modelled one (5h), and a cached or stale API response reports the cycle time rather than the age of the data it is reporting on -- while UsageData.stale already knows the reading may be old.

Scope: add a poll-time field to UsageData (src/poller.rs:236-260), populate it at the poll site, and use it for PrevUsageSnapshot.taken_at instead of the cycle's now. The formatters in src/governor.rs need no change -- they already take prev_at/curr_at as arguments.

This was left out of bf-3r0is deliberately: it is a production data-model change touching the poller, not a formatting fix, and it needs its own decision about what a poll timestamp means for cached responses.

Acceptance criteria:
- UsageData carries the instant the reading was taken, populated at the real poll site
- PrevUsageSnapshot.taken_at comes from that field rather than the cycle's Utc::now()
- A test drives two cycles with fixture readings whose poll times are hours apart and asserts the rendered Delta-t matches the fixture interval, not the wall-clock gap between cycles
- cargo test passes (use ~/.cargo/bin/cargo)

issue.description:
Follow-up from bf-5q0qv, which could not get a CNPG backup in ns forgejo to reach Completed.

Cluster: iad-ci (~/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig), ns forgejo, cluster forgejo-postgres. 831 of 832 Backup objects are phase=failed; the single completed one is forgejo-postgres-daily-20260806150300 (2026-08-06T15:03Z), predating the current config.

TWO stacked defects:

1) HARD CONFIG BUG (current, exit status 3). declarative-config commit d89f8e32 set
   spec.backup.barmanObjectStore.data.additionalCommandArgs: ["--min-chunk-size=5G"]
   for BOTH k8s/iad-ci/forgejo/cnpg-cluster.yaml and k8s/iad-ci/queue-db/cnpg-cluster.yaml.
   barman rejects it before doing any work:
     barman-cloud-backup: error: argument --min-chunk-size: '5G' is not a valid size string
   Verified in-pod against barman.clients.cloud_backup.check_size:
     '5G' -> REJECTED;  '1024MB' -> 1073741824;  '5GB' -> 5368709120;  '2GB' -> 2147483648
   Every backup since 2026-08-07T04:03Z fails this way. A valid-size edit to '1024MB' is
   currently sitting UNCOMMITTED in the declarative-config working tree (forgejo file only;
   queue-db still has 5G committed). That edit is necessary but NOT sufficient -- see (2).

2) ROOT CAUSE (pre-existing, exit status 1). Before the 5G arg landed, backups failed with:
     InvalidPartSize: Part size 4837376 is not a multiple of the block size (65536 bytes).
     ARMOR's uniform-part-size contract (ADR-005) requires block-aligned parts.
   The premise behind d89f8e32 -- and behind the pending 1024MB edit -- is that raising
   min-chunk-size above the backup size yields a single part, and that 'ADR-005 allows the
   final part to be short'. THAT PREMISE IS FALSE. Probed ARMOR directly via boto3 multipart
   from inside forgejo-postgres-1 on 2026-08-07:
     single misaligned part (4837376 B)          -> FAIL InvalidPartSize
     single aligned part (4849664 B = 65536*74)  -> OK
     aligned first part + short final (1000 B)   -> FAIL InvalidPartSize (on the FINAL part)
     misaligned first + short final              -> FAIL InvalidPartSize
   So ARMOR requires EVERY part, including the sole/final part, to be a multiple of 65536.
   No standard S3 client can satisfy that -- a short final part is normal S3 semantics.
   Forcing a single part just makes one misaligned part instead of several; the forgejo DB is
   only 40 MB, so 1024MB would produce exactly one ~40MB part that is almost certainly not a
   multiple of 65536 and will still be rejected.

Note: WAL archiving (barman-cloud-wal-archive) is unaffected and working -- it does not use
multipart upload.

Recommended fix (pick one, in order of preference):
  a) Relax ARMOR ADR-005 to accept a short final part (standard S3 CompleteMultipartUpload
     semantics). This is the only option that makes ARMOR usable by unmodified S3 clients.
  b) Have ARMOR zero-pad the final part server-side to the block size and record the true
     object length.
  c) Point forgejo/queue-db CNPG backups at an S3 endpoint without the alignment contract.
Whatever is chosen, also correct the invalid '5G' size string in both cnpg-cluster.yaml files
so the failure mode stops masking the real one.

Acceptance criteria:
- A Backup object in ns forgejo reaches status.phase == completed with the current config.
- queue-db backups likewise verified, or explicitly stated as out of scope.
- The ARMOR alignment probe above re-run and showing a short final part is accepted.

## Task: Safe Mode — Automatic Conservatism

When prediction accuracy degrades, enter a conservative fallback mode.

### What to Implement
- In `src/governor.rs` (extend):
  - `check_safe_mode(calibration: &CalibrationState, config: &SafeModeConfig) -> SafeModeState`
  - Entry conditions (OR):
    - Median prediction error > enter_median_error (default 10.0%)
    - Prediction error stddev > enter_stddev (default 15.0%)
  - Effects while active:
    - target_utilization reduced by util_reduction (default 0.10) — e.g. 0.90 -> 0.80
    - hysteresis_band widened by hysteresis_boost (default 1)
    - Sprint disabled
    - Cross-window optimization disabled (fall back to binding-window)
    - Always use p75 (worst-case) from confidence cone
  - Exit conditions (ALL must be true):
    - Median error < exit_median_error (default 7.0%)
    - Stddev < exit_stddev (default 12.0%)
    - At least 3 new predictions scored since entry
  - Hysteresis between entry/exit thresholds prevents toggling
  - State: safe_mode.active, entered_at, trigger, median_error_at_entry, predictions_since_entry

issue.notes:
[migrated comment from docs-5h2j, 2026-04-15T14:29:48Z, author coding]
Wrote a zero-usage heartbeat fleet record in run_collection_pass() when session_usage is empty (no new data). Previously the early return skipped the database write, letting the governor's freshness check see a stale t1 timestamp and fire false collector_offline alerts during idle periods.

## Retrospective
- **What worked:** Reading the systemd journal to pinpoint the exact 6-minute gap (10:03:49–10:09:49) where three consecutive 'no new usage data' passes left the fleet aggregate stale, confirming the diagnosis without guessing.
- **What didn't:** Nothing failed — the fix was straightforward once the idle-period gap was confirmed in the logs.
- **Surprise:** The standalone collector service and the governor's embedded collector both run run_collection_pass() independently, so the same idle gap appears in both service logs. The fix covers both paths since they share the same function.
- **Reusable pattern:** When a daemon has a liveness freshness check downstream, any early-return code path that skips the normal heartbeat write will cause false offline alerts. Always write a heartbeat record on every successful pass, even if there is nothing substantive to report.

  "Part size <n> is not a multiple of the block size (65536 bytes)" (InvalidPartSize) and the
  UploadPart / CompleteMultipartUpload path it sits on.
- Read ADR-005 (uniform part size). Determine what the alignment contract actually exists for --
  e.g. erasure coding, striping, or offset arithmetic that assumes every part is block-aligned --
  and what breaks if the final part is short.
- Evaluate the three candidate fixes from the parent bead:
  a) Relax ADR-005 to accept a short FINAL part (standard S3 semantics). Preferred -- the only
     option that makes ARMOR usable by unmodified S3 clients.
  b) Zero-pad the final part server-side to the block size, recording the true object length so
     GET/HEAD/Range return the unpadded bytes.
  c) Point forgejo/queue-db CNPG backups at a different S3 endpoint without the contract.
- For (a) and (b), state concretely what changes: which invariant is weakened, how existing
  objects stay readable, whether Range reads and the erasure/stripe layer need changes, and
  whether stored metadata needs a new field for true length.

Acceptance criteria:
- File/function references (path:line) for the validator and for ADR-005.
- A written explanation of WHY the alignment invariant exists.
- One option explicitly chosen, with rationale and the rejected options' reasons.
- If (c) is chosen, the alternative endpoint is named and confirmed reachable from ns forgejo.
issue.notes:
[migrated notes from bf-59kyr]
Located validation code and completed decision analysis.

## Code Locations
- UploadPart validation: handlers.go:2271-2274 (block alignment check)
- CompleteMultipartUpload backstop: handlers.go:2556-2560
- ADR-005: docs/adr/005-out-of-order-multipart-uniform-part-size.md

## Why Alignment Exists
ARMOR uses AES-256 CTR mode with offset formula: offset(N) = (N-1) × P / BlockSize
This requires P (uniform part size) to be block-aligned (65536 bytes) so part 2+ start on block boundaries. Misalignment corrupts CTR keystream and HMAC indices → silent data corruption.

## Part 1 and Final Part Exemptions
- Part 1: Always starts at block 0, so (1-1)×P/BlockSize = 0 for any P
- Final part: Nothing follows it, partial trailing block is ordinary
- These exemptions are CORRECT, not concessions (ADR-011 2026-08-07)

## Decision: CHOSEN OPTION (a)
Relax ADR-005 to accept short final part via the already-implemented exemptions from ADR-011:
- Part 1 may be any size (pins P, marks upload single-part-only if non-aligned)
- Presumed-final part (size < P) may be any size
- Regular parts remain fully block-aligned

Rationale:
1. Already implemented in ARMOR commit fc6c1a86
2. Correct reading of the contract (ADR-011)
3. Standard S3 semantics (short final parts are normal)
4. No format/metadata change needed
5. Resolves immediate outage with single-part barman config

## Rejected Options
(b) Zero-padding: Unnecessary complexity, needs new metadata field
(c) Different endpoint (Garage): Contradicts ADR-1 operator direction

## Critical Finding from bf-3i9nr
Probe revealed ARMOR multipart uploads are completely broken (InternalError/InvalidPart), not just alignment-validated. The exemptions are necessary but not sufficient—child 4 must investigate broader multipart failure.

Full decision documented in decision plan (not a git artifact, per bead instructions).

issue.description:
The annotation guard at src/governor.rs (~line 5578) compares two DIFFERENT quantities, so the 'worker count changed mid-interval' guard fires spuriously and annotation is skipped in production even though all unit tests pass.

workers_at_start = state.last_fleet_aggregate.sonnet_workers  (collector's SONNET-only worker count, src/state.rs:182)
workers_at_end   = current_total = total_tmux_count as u32    (src/governor.rs:5367 - total tmux sessions across ALL model classes)

Whenever the fleet runs any non-sonnet worker these differ every cycle, annotation_skip_reason() returns WorkerCountChanged, and annotate_window_pct_deltas() is never called. Existing unit tests do not catch this because they call annotation_skip_reason()/annotate_window_pct_deltas() directly with matching, hand-supplied counts.

Fix: compare like with like. Either pass the sonnet-only worker count for both ends, or the all-model total for both ends - whichever matches the population of the i rows being annotated (the collector's i records). Document the choice in a comment at the call site.

Acceptance criteria:
- workers_at_start and workers_at_end are the same quantity, measured the same way
- Comment at the call site states which population is used and why it matches the annotated i rows
- Regression test: a cycle with a steady fleet that includes non-sonnet workers does NOT trigger the WorkerCountChanged skip
- cargo test passes

Call site governor.rs:5614 uses it for both the guard and the db::annotate_window_pct_deltas call. The tmux census (current_total) is no longer referenced there.

2. Comment present at call site (governor.rs:5608-5612) plus the full rationale on annotation_worker_counts.

Build the token collector daemon that tails Claude Code JSONL session files and captures model-specific, token-type-specific consumption data.

  - Walk ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl for unprocessed lines

- SQLite mirror with tables: i, f, w (wide schemas matching JSONL record types)

- cgov collect CLI subcommand (standalone, no daemon required)
- cgov collect --daemon mode (continuous loop)
- cgov token-history query subcommands (--last, --compare, --fleet, --rebuild-db)

- Dollar computation against known API pricing (each tok_type x model)
- Delta verification (second pass emits zero-n records)

- Fleet variance stats with synthetic data

- Plan: /home/coding/claude-governor/docs/plan/plan.md (Phase 1b, lines 1498-1535)
- Token type pricing table in plan (Component 2)
- Record format examples in plan (i, f, w types)

issue.description:
## Symptom

A NEEDLE worker using the claude-print-opus adapter timed out on 46% of its
dispatches (26 of 57), including SIX consecutive 20-minute timeouts on a single
bead (bf-3t7xa) — two hours of Opus burned for no output.

## Root cause

The dispatched `claude` attaches to the VS Code extension host instead of ever
reaching the API.

Evidence from a hung dispatch:

- Its ONLY socket was loopback: 127.0.0.1 -> 127.0.0.1:54964, owned by
  `node ... bootstrap-fork --type=extensionHost` (VS Code Server).
- `~/.claude/ide/54964.lock` exists — the port matches exactly, so this is IDE
  discovery, not coincidence.
- Socket idle time climbed 639,620ms -> 728,508ms across samples with
  bytes_received frozen at 5,600. CPU was 50ms per 30s, state S, wchan
  do_epoll_wait.
- NO outbound connection to the API. Healthy sibling agents all held
  connections to the proxy on :8444; this one never opened one.

It attaches because it inherits `CLAUDECODE=1` plus `VSCODE_IPC_HOOK_CLI` from
whatever launched the worker. `CLAUDECODE=1` tells a nested Claude Code it is
running inside Claude Code, and the lockfile gives it an extension host to
connect to. It then blocks there until NEEDLE's 1200s claude-print backstop
fires.

## Why the other adapter is immune

The glm adapter's dispatch command explicitly scrubs this:

    cd <workspace> && git rev-parse HEAD > .needle-predispatch-sha; unset CLAUDECODE; ...

The claude-print-opus adapter's invoke_template does not:

    cd {workspace} && /home/coding/.local/bin/claude-print --model {model} \
      --max-turns 100 --output-format stream-json --dangerously-skip-permissions \
      --no-inherit-hooks < {prompt_file}

## Deliverables

- Add `unset CLAUDECODE` to the invoke_template in the claude-print-{opus,fable}
  adapters, matching the glm adapter.
- Also unset the VS Code IPC vars (VSCODE_IPC_HOOK_CLI at minimum) so the agent
  cannot discover an extension host regardless of launch context.
- Update the committed copies under deploy/needle-adapters/ and document the
  requirement in CLAUDE.md section 3 alongside the existing two hard-won rules
  (prompt via `< {prompt_file}`, absolute binary path). This is a third one of
  the same kind.

## Acceptance criteria

- A worker launched from an interactive Claude Code session (CLAUDECODE=1 and a
  live VSCODE_IPC_HOOK_CLI in the environment) dispatches agents that open an
  API connection and never connect to any ~/.claude/ide/*.lock port.
- Timeout rate over a >=20-dispatch run returns to baseline.

## Notes

Production workers launched by cgov via systemd get a clean environment and so
do not hit this — it surfaces when a worker is started from inside an
interactive Claude Code shell. The adapter should be immune either way.

# bf-4qd6k — Final gate: cargo test + br-to-bf sweep results

Final gate and bookkeeping for the `br create` default-alert-command fix
(umbrella parent: bf-1hbmk). Date: 2026-08-06.

This bead is the *gate*, not the investigation. Sibling bf-3g1ns assembled the
combined narrative onto bf-1hbmk from bf-5ke9f / bf-10l6i / bf-6bicx. Everything
below was re-verified first-hand here rather than inherited, because the whole
point of a final gate is that it does not take the earlier children's word for it.

## VERDICT

**Test suite passes. Zero files needed an edit during this final sweep.** Every
`br create` occurrence in the stated scope had already been cleared by an earlier
commit. The sweep confirmed the fix rather than performing it.

## CARGO TEST GATE — PASS

Run as `~/.cargo/bin/cargo test` with the **absolute path**, deliberately not bare
`cargo`: the wrapper on PATH discards stderr and exits 0 even on failure, so a bare
invocation is not a gate at all. Verified twice — once piped for the log, once with
output discarded to read the real exit status (piping loses it to the last stage).

```
~/.cargo/bin/cargo test  ->  exit code 0
```

| Metric | Result |
|---|---|
| Test targets | 18, all `test result: ok.` |
| Passed | 849 |
| Failed | **0** |
| Ignored | 8 (5 doc-tests, 3 integration) |

- Main lib suite: `750 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored` (finished in 9.91s)
- 16 integration targets: all `test result: ok.`, 0 failed
- Doc-tests: `17 passed; 0 failed; 5 ignored`
- No `FAILED`, no `panicked`, no `failures:`, no `error[` anywhere in the log.

No failures, so no follow-up bead filed. Pre-existing build warnings are **out of
scope and untouched**: ~20 unused-import/unused-variable warnings in test modules,
1 unused doc comment, and 3 unnecessary-parentheses warnings in
`src/governor.rs:7207/7213/7219`. None are regressions from this fix.

## GREP GATE — 0 HITS

```
grep -rn 'br create' src/ docs/ config/ scripts/        -> 0 hits, exit 1
grep -rnE '\bbr[[:space:]]+create' src/ docs/ config/ scripts/ -> 0 hits, exit 1
```

The whitespace-tolerant variant is run alongside the literal so that `br  create`
or a tab-separated form cannot slip through the literal-string check.

## PER-TARGET: NEEDED AN EDIT vs. ALREADY CORRECT

| # | Target | Needed edit? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `config/governor.yaml` | **No** — correct by inheritance | verified here |
| 2 | `~/.config/claude-governor/governor.yaml` | **No** — correct by inheritance | verified here |
| 3 | `src/` | **No** — already clean | fixed earlier by 8b08f68 |
| 4 | `docs/` | **Yes — 2 files**, by earlier children | 1698c92, f3ba946 |
| 5 | `config/` (dir-wide) | **No** — never had a hit | `git log -S` empty |
| 6 | `scripts/` | **No** — never had a hit | `git log -S` empty |

### 1. `config/governor.yaml` — NO EDIT NEEDED, correct by inheritance

The `alerts:` block at line 162 declares exactly six keys — `enabled`,
`cooldown_minutes`, `min_severity`, `low_cache_eff_threshold`,
`low_cache_eff_intervals`, `auto_bead`. There is **no explicit `command:` key**,
so the value comes from `default_alert_command()`. `grep -n 'br'` over the whole
file returns nothing (exit 1) — not just no `br create`, but no `br` at all.

### 2. `~/.config/claude-governor/governor.yaml` — NO EDIT NEEDED, correct by inheritance

The live config's `alerts:` block at line 135 carries the identical six keys, also
with **no explicit `command:` key**, and inherits the same default. `grep -n 'br'`
likewise returns nothing. Worth stating plainly: this is the file that would
actually be read at runtime, so "the repo config is clean" would not by itself have
closed the question. It was checked directly.

### 3. `src/` — NO EDIT NEEDED, already clean

The single `br create` in code was fixed by **8b08f68** (2026-08-03, the
`src/config.rs` default alert command) — *before* the bf-4qd6k split existed.
**78fe193** then added the regression test.

### 4. `docs/` — EDITED (2 files), by earlier children

- **1698c92** fixed `docs/research/alerts.md:185` (bf-482rd)
- **f3ba946** fixed `docs/plan/plan.md:1692` (bf-5wdrk)

Zero hits remain. These two are the only genuine edits the whole sweep produced.

### 5–6. `config/`, `scripts/` — NO EDIT NEEDED, never had a hit

`git log -S'br create' -- config/` and `-- scripts/` both return no commits;
`scripts/polish-seeder.sh:104` already used `bf create`.

## REGRESSION GUARD

Re-read first-hand at `src/config.rs`:

```rust
fn default_alert_command() -> Vec<String> {          // line 569
    vec!["bf", "create", "--type", "human"]          // (to_string() elided)
}

fn test_default_alert_command_uses_bf() {            // line 1310
    let cmd = default_alert_command();
    assert_eq!(cmd[0], "bf");
    assert_eq!(cmd, vec!["bf", "create", "--type", "human"]);
    assert_eq!(AlertConfig::default().command[0], "bf");
}
```

`AlertConfig.command` is `#[serde(default = "default_alert_command")]`. The test
pins both the first element and the full vector, and separately pins
`AlertConfig::default()`, so the deprecated `br` shim cannot silently reappear
through the default path. Since both YAML files rely on that default rather than
overriding it, this test is what actually protects them.

## OUT-OF-SCOPE `br` REFERENCES — DELIBERATELY NOT EDITED

- `.beads/issues.jsonl` still matches `br create` on 10 lines (bf-1hbmk, bf-1o5in,
  bf-47asm, bf-482rd, bf-4qd6k, bf-5ke9f, bf-5wdrk, bf-6bicx, docs-7d4, docs-ycf).
  Each is inside a bead title/description that *names the bug*. Rewriting them
  would edit the audit trail to erase the record of the thing being fixed.
- Non-`create` `br` subcommands survive as captured shell transcripts in
  `docs/pluck-query-results.md:196,206,227,235` and
  `docs/bf-wvljm-bead-inventory.md:181`. These are historical transcripts, not
  instructions to follow.

Purging every remaining `br` reference is separate work and deserves its own bead;
it is not in this umbrella's stated scope.

## False Positive Analysis

**Alert:** emergency_brake_activated (CRITICAL)
**Activated:** 2026-04-23T01:21:03Z
**Bead:** docs-1w6q

### Evidence of false positive

- seven_day window at 100% utilization, margin_hrs=-7.2h, 7.2h remaining
- seven_day_sonnet window at 86% utilization, 7.2h remaining
- Workers at 0 (emergency brake scaled fleet to 0 on activation)
- No active burn — brake itself prevents any token consumption
- Utilization pinned at 100% because with zero workers, no consumption occurs to change the ratio; the window will reset naturally in ~7.2h

### Root cause

Same as prior false positives (docs-3wbo, docs-j5w0, docs-md2q, docs-unw6): the emergency brake triggers at 98% utilization, kills all workers, and then utilization cannot decrease because there's no consumption to shift the ratio. The alert re-fires every 60 minutes (cooldown) until the seven_day window resets.

### Status

False positive — no action required. The window will reset and the brake will clear automatically.

issue.description:
## Task: Target Worker Computation with Hysteresis

Implement compute_target_workers() and the hysteresis band that prevents scaling oscillation.

### What to Implement
- In `src/governor.rs` (new module):
  - `compute_target_workers(usage, schedule, burn_rate, config) -> u32`:
    - Compute target_ceiling per window from target_utilization
    - remaining_capacity = max(0, target_ceiling - current_pct)
    - target_rate_per_effective_hour = remaining_capacity / effective_hours_remaining
    - target_rate_per_raw_hour = target_rate_per_effective_hour * current_multiplier
    - target_workers = floor(target_rate / burn_rate_per_worker_per_hour)
    - Clamp to [min_workers, max_workers] per agent
    - Use safe_worker_count[binding_window] as ceiling
  - `should_scale(current: u32, target: u32, hysteresis_band: u32) -> ScaleAction`:
    - If current < target - band: scale up
    - If current > target + band: scale down
    - Else: no action (within dead band)
  - `ScaleAction` enum: ScaleUp(u32), ScaleDown(u32), NoAction
  - Default hysteresis_band = 1 (only act when deviation >= 2 workers)
  - Multi-agent: aggregate burn across all enabled agents; scale down highest-cost agent first

### Files
- `src/governor.rs` (new module, partial — main loop in separate task)
- `src/main.rs` (add `mod governor`)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: target computation with known inputs matches hand calculation
- Unit test: hysteresis — target=3, current=4, band=1 -> no action
- Unit test: hysteresis — target=3, current=5, band=1 -> scale down 2
- Unit test: clamping to min/max workers
- Unit test: binding window ceiling overrides target
- Unit test: multi-agent scale-down prefers highest-cost agent

### Acceptance Criteria
- Correct formula matching plan specification
- Hysteresis prevents oscillation on small deviations
- Binding window safe_worker_count acts as hard ceiling
- Multi-agent cost-based scale-down ordering
- All edge cases (zero remaining, past-ceiling) handled

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P3 fleet EMA (docs-5bu) — needs capacity forecast
- Depends on: P2 schedule calculator (docs-6dm) — needs effective hours
issue.title: P4: Target worker computation with hysteresis

Implement the WindowRecord struct and the forecast computation for all three windows.

### Files to Modify
- `src/collector.rs` — add WindowRecord and forecast logic

### What to Implement
- `pub struct WindowRecord` with all schema fields:
  - `r: String` (always "w"), `ts: DateTime<Utc>`, `win: String` (window name: "five_hour", "seven_day", "seven_day_sonnet")
  - `pk: bool`, `ceil: f64` (target ceiling from config, e.g. 90.0)
  - `snap: f64` (raw platform utilization %), `reset: DateTime<Utc>` (window reset time)
  - `delta: f64` (pct change this interval), `remain: f64` (`ceil - snap`, NOT `100 - snap`)
  - `hrs_left: f64` (hours until reset), `fleet_pct_hr: f64` (fleet burn rate as pct/hr)
  - `exh_hrs: f64` (`remain / fleet_pct_hr`), `cutoff_risk: u8` (1 if `exh_hrs < hrs_left`)
  - `margin_hrs: f64` (`hrs_left - exh_hrs`)
  - `bind: u8` (1 if most constrained), `safe_w: Option<u32>` (only on binding window)
- `pub fn compute_window_forecast(win: &str, snap: f64, ceil: f64, reset: DateTime<Utc>, now: DateTime<Utc>, fleet_pct_hr: f64, pk: bool) -> WindowRecord`:
  - Compute all derived fields: remain, hrs_left, exh_hrs, cutoff_risk, margin_hrs

### Test Command

cargo test --lib collector::tests::window_forecast 2>&1; echo "EXIT: $?"

issue.close_reason:
Implemented in commit 74dd4de: alert dedup is now a stateful per-episode lifecycle instead of a cooldown timer. An episode is one continuous stretch during which a condition holds, keyed by alert type + scope. First cycle true -> create ONE bead and store its id in governor-state.json under open_alert_beads; while it stays true -> no new bead, refresh the existing one's notes at most once per cooldown_minutes; first cycle not true -> auto-close the bead with a reason and drop the entry. cooldown_minutes survives only as an anti-flap floor on OPENING a new episode after one resolves, so a flapping condition still cannot mint a bead per toggle. Bead volume is now bounded by distinct incidents rather than elapsed time -- the structural cause of the 226 sonnet_cutoff_risk / 160 cutoff_imminent bead pileup.

Touches: state (OpenAlertBead + open_alert_beads, serde default so existing state files load unchanged), alerts (AlertCondition scope + episode_key, fire_alert returns the bead id, new close_alert_bead/refresh_alert_bead/process_alert_episodes), config (close_command/update_command; create command now 'bf create --json --type human --title' so the id is parseable), governor (cycle 8 drives it; FP telemetry now records once per episode, measuring incidents not cooldown windows), status display (lists open episodes with bead ids).

alerts.auto_bead stays false -- the <5% FP-rate gate from docs-878a is untouched. What changed is that re-enabling it can no longer reproduce the spam, since the failure mode was structural.

Verified this pass: all 20 test targets pass, 0 failed (781 in the lib suite); the end-to-end test runs against the real bf 0.4.0 CLI and confirms one bead created, refreshed in place, then auto-closed; alerts.rs and state.rs are fmt-clean; no new clippy warnings.

CAVEAT: commit is local only. git.ardenone.com has been returning 503 'no available server' for the entire forge (root URL included) across many attempts; main is 25 commits ahead of origin/main. Filed bf-4najn (P1) to track pushing the backlog once the host recovers. The work is complete and committed; only the push is outstanding.
issue.description: src/alerts.rs::should_fire()/process_alerts() dedup purely on a per-alert-type cooldown timer (default 60 minutes, alerts.cooldown_minutes in governor.yaml): while a condition remains true past the cooldown window, fire_alert() creates a brand-new bead via the configured command every time the cooldown elapses, rather than tracking one open bead per distinct condition episode. Historical bead data in this repo's own .beads workspace bears this out: bf list --json shows 226 closed beads titled starting with '[WARNING] sonnet_cutoff_risk' and 160 titled '[CRITICAL] cutoff_imminent' (out of 517 total issue_type=human alert beads created historically), almost certainly representing far fewer distinct real incidents than that count of beads. Redesign the alert lifecycle: on first firing of a given (alert_type, window) condition, create one bead and remember its bead id in governor-state.json (e.g. under alert_cooldown or a new open_alert_beads map); on subsequent cycles where the condition is still true, update/comment on the existing bead instead of creating a new one (or simply suppress, since the bead is already open and visible); when the condition clears, auto-close the bead. This is a natural extension of the auto_bead FP-rate gating work already done (see docs-878a, notes/bf-h7toj.md, and the alert_fp_telemetry struct in src/state.rs which already tracks true/false-positive outcomes per alert type) and should be done as part of re-enabling alerts.auto_bead so re-enablement doesn't reproduce the original spam problem. issue.description: governor.yaml's alerts.auto_bead comment states the re-enablement criterion: 'Re-enable only after FP rate < 5% over 100-alert window.' The AlertFpTelemetry struct in src/state.rs already tracks recorded sample count, false-positive count, and aggregate FP rate per alert type, and cgov status --json already emits it as the alert_fp_telemetry field, but there is no human-facing view of progress toward the 100-sample threshold - an operator has to know to grep the JSON. Add a doctor check in src/doctor.rs, or a small new cgov alerts subcommand, that reports per alert type: samples recorded so far, current FP rate, and how many more samples are needed before the 100-sample / 5-percent-FP re-enablement bar is met, so there is a visible trackable path back to auto_bead true instead of the setting being indefinitely stuck at false with no visible momentum. Note this telemetry currently only accumulates while the governor daemon (the hidden _daemon subcommand) is actually running and evaluating alert conditions each cycle, so this is most useful once the daemon is confirmed running again (see the separate bead about the currently stopped daemon, bf-hjage) and complements the stateful alert dedup bead bf-5k6yv and ADR-001 in docs/plan/plan.md.
issue.title: Surface alert_fp_telemetry re-enablement progress in cgov doctor / a new cgov alerts view

issue.description:
## Task: Daemon Management — systemd and tmux Modes

Implement cgov start/stop/restart/enable/disable with dual-mode daemon management.

### What to Implement
- In `src/daemon.rs` (new module):
  - Mode detection: check for systemd user session availability
  - **Mode A: systemd user service** (Linux default):
    - `cgov enable`: install unit files, daemon-reload, enable + start both services
    - `cgov disable`: stop + disable both services
    - `cgov start`: start services (must be enabled first)
    - `cgov stop`: graceful stop (governor finishes current cycle)
    - `cgov restart`: stop + start
    - Unit files: claude-governor.service and claude-token-collector.service
  - **Mode B: tmux sessions** (fallback):
    - `cgov start`: `tmux new-session -d -s "claude-governor" "cgov _daemon"` (and token-collector)
    - `cgov stop`: send SIGTERM to tmux session processes
  - `_daemon` internal subcommand: the actual daemon entrypoint (used by both modes)
  - `_token-collector` internal subcommand: token collector entrypoint
  - Store chosen mode in governor.yaml as `daemon_mode: systemd|tmux`
  - `cgov logs --follow` works with both modes (tails log file directly)

### Files
- `src/daemon.rs` (new module)
- `systemd/claude-governor.service` (template)
- `systemd/claude-token-collector.service` (template)
- `src/main.rs` (add daemon subcommands)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: systemd detection logic
- Unit test: service file installation to correct path (~/.config/systemd/user/)
- Unit test: tmux fallback creates correct sessions
- Unit test: stop waits for current cycle completion

### Acceptance Criteria
- Auto-detects systemd vs tmux
- Services survive reboot when enabled via systemd
- tmux fallback works on systems without systemd
- Graceful stop ensures no mid-cycle interruption
- Logs accessible regardless of daemon mode

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P4 main daemon loop (docs-4f7) — needs _daemon entrypoint
issue.title: P6: Daemon management — systemd and tmux modes

issue.description:
## Task: Prediction Accuracy Self-Calibration

Track prediction accuracy and auto-tune governor parameters based on historical performance.

### What to Implement
- New `src/calibrator.rs` module:
  - `score_prediction(window, predicted_pct, actual_pct) -> PredictionScore`:
    - `prediction_error = actual_final_pct - predicted_final_pct`
    - Negative = conservative, positive = aggressive
    - `correct`: predicted exhaustion matched actual
  - Append scored predictions to `~/.needle/state/prediction-accuracy.jsonl`
  - Hook into window reset events to trigger scoring
  - `CalibrationState`: predictions_scored, median_error per window, auto-tuned params
  - Auto-tuning rules (activated after >= 10 scored predictions per window):
    - Median error < -5 (conservative): increase burn_rate_alpha +0.02, widen hysteresis +0.5
    - Median error > +5 (aggressive): decrease alpha -0.02, tighten hysteresis -0.5
    - Stddev > 10 (unpredictable): lower target_utilization -0.02
  - Clamp ranges: alpha [0.05, 0.5], hysteresis [0, 3], target_util [0.70, 0.98]
  - Write calibration state to governor-state.json
  - Auto-tuning opt-in via `calibration.auto_calibrate: true` in config

### Files
- `src/calibrator.rs` (new module)
- `src/main.rs` (add `mod calibrator`)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: scoring with known prediction/actual pairs
- Unit test: auto-tuning direction — conservative data increases alpha
- Unit test: auto-tuning direction — aggressive data decreases alpha
- Unit test: clamp enforcement at boundaries
- Unit test: no tuning until 10 predictions scored
- Unit test: JSONL append format

### Acceptance Criteria
- Prediction accuracy tracked per window
- Auto-tuning adjusts parameters in correct direction
- Clamps prevent runaway parameter drift
- Opt-in via config (tracking always active, tuning optional)
- JSONL file serves as audit trail

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P3 fleet EMA (docs-5bu) — needs capacity forecast to score
- Depends on: P3 state store (docs-thy) — writes calibration state
issue.title: P7: Prediction accuracy self-calibration

Add a pure helper next to calculate_window_pct_delta:

    pub fn format_window_deltas(
        prev: &crate::db::WindowPctSnapshot,
        curr: &crate::db::WindowPctSnapshot,
        prev_at: chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>,
        curr_at: chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>,
    ) -> String

It returns one readable line carrying the window labels (5h / 7d / 7ds), the signed percentage deltas, the previous and current percentages, and both snapshot timestamps. Do not call log:: inside it and do not touch the cycle paths yet — wiring is the next bead.

Acceptance criteria:
- format_window_deltas exists in src/governor.rs and is pure (returns String, no logging, no I/O)
- Output names all three windows and shows signed deltas (e.g. 5h=+2.50%)
- Output includes both snapshot timestamps
- Unit tests assert the rendered string for a positive-delta case and a negative-delta case
- cargo test passes; cargo clippy clean

Unknown model "claude-sonnet-5", falling back to ... for pricing — add it to governor.yaml' (src/pricing.rs:138). Add a claude-sonnet-5 entry (and check for claude-opus-5 and claude-haiku-5 equivalents) to config/governor.yaml's pricing models block with correct per-model-token-type rates (input, output, two cache write tiers, cache read), and update the live ~/.config/claude-governor/governor.yaml on this host the same way. Consider whether this class of drift (pricing config falling behind model releases) warrants a doctor check that fails loudly, not just warns in logs, when a large share of recent collector passes hit the fallback path.
