issue.description:
git.ardenone.com has returned HTTP 503 'no available server' for all operations since ~2026-08-07T01:43Z, blocking every 'git push origin' from this and other repos on the host.

Root cause (verified twice, 07:20 and 07:45 UTC 2026-08-07): pod forgejo-gitea-769476465f-njdc5 in namespace 'forgejo' of cluster iad-ci (reachable via ~/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig) is 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff, 55 restarts, pod age 7d12h. It aborts fatally on every start:

  modules/storage/minio.go:97 NewMinioStorage() [I] Creating Minio storage at armor.armor.svc.cluster.local:9000:iad-ci with base path forgejo/storage/attachments/
  routers/init.go:62 mustInit() [F] code.gitea.io/gitea/modules/storage.Init failed: permission denied

Forgejo 10.0.0+gitea-1.22.0 fails initialising its MinIO/S3 attachment storage. In gitea 1.22 that path is BucketExists/MakeBucket, and 'permission denied' is convertMinioErr's mapping of S3 AccessDenied. Traefik therefore has zero healthy endpoints behind the git.ardenone.com IngressRoute, which is why Cloudflare Tunnel returns 503 -- the tunnel and Traefik are fine, the backend is dead.

Supporting evidence:
- Config: forgejo-application.yml sets [storage] and [lfs] STORAGE_TYPE=minio, MINIO_ENDPOINT=armor.armor.svc.cluster.local:9000, MINIO_BUCKET=iad-ci. Credentials come from secret forgejo-backup-armor (keys auth-access-key / auth-secret-key).
- The credential is present and fresh: all 5 externalsecrets in ns forgejo report SecretSynced/True.
- ARMOR itself is UP and serving that same bucket: pod armor-69cdbb4d46-24d22 1/1 Running, thousands of status-200 requests including GETs under /iad-ci/forgejo/. So this is a bucket-level authz regression (HEAD bucket / MakeBucket on 'iad-ci' denied) rather than an ARMOR outage, while prefixed object GET/PUT for the same credential succeeds.
- Probably the same regression: CNPG backups in ns forgejo are also failing ('Backup failed' events for forgejo-postgres-daily-* and forgejo-postgres-test-manual).
- postgres-1, forgejo-init and forgejo-backup pods are all 1/1 Running; only the web/git app is down.

Fix belongs in the ardenone-cluster / declarative-config domain, NOT in claude-governor: restore the bucket-level S3 permission for the forgejo-backup-armor credential on bucket 'iad-ci' in the ARMOR object store, or reconfigure Forgejo's storage backend. Deliberately not done unilaterally from a claude-governor bead -- it is a production authz change in a separate system.

Impact while open: no repo on this host can push to origin. claude-governor specifically is 28 commits ahead of origin/main (local 50f1fc7, origin/main 7a06f2d); those commits were rescued to the GitHub mirror under bf-4najn, but other repos may not have a mirror and remain stranded.

Acceptance criteria:
- curl https://git.ardenone.com/ returns 200
- forgejo-gitea pod is 1/1 Running with 0 recent restarts
- 'git push origin main' from /home/coding/claude-governor advances origin/main to the local HEAD
- CNPG backups in ns forgejo succeed again

Branch: fix/bf-2fvmp-forgejo-gitea-reloader @ df2862a2 (pushed to origin)
File: k8s/iad-ci/forgejo/forgejo-application.yml (repo jedarden/declarative-config)
ArgoCD targetRevision is HEAD, so the branch cannot auto-sync. main is untouched.

== BOTH PRESCRIBED OPTIONS REJECTED ON A DISPROVEN PREMISE ==
Option A (add s3:ListBucket / s3:CreateBucket to a forgejo-backup-armor policy):
IMPOSSIBLE, not merely wrong. Per bf-385rj, ARMOR is a bespoke single-bucket S3
gateway with no IAM action model. Authz is Credential.ACLs, checked by CheckACL
(auth.go:293-317) only from server.go:715/904 on object paths. HeadBucket and
CreateBucket are not ACL-gated at all; the single credential has ACLs: nil =
full access to bucket iad-ci. There is no policy document, CR, or ExternalSecret
-fed policy doc anywhere to patch. No file exists to write the diff into.

Option B (repoint MINIO_BUCKET, or STORAGE_TYPE=local for attachments):
REJECTED. ARMOR serves exactly one bucket (iad-ci), so there is no other bucket
to point at. STORAGE_TYPE=local would let the pod boot only by abandoning the
object store: orphans existing attachments/LFS under iad-ci/forgejo/, needs a
data migration plus PVC headroom on a 20Gi RWO volume, and leaves the real
defect in place to recur at the next rotation. It converts a stale-config bug
into a storage-architecture change.

Add reloader.stakater.com/auto: "true" via deployment.annotations.

Root cause (bf-1tkap/bf-385rj): the chart renders /data/gitea/conf/app.ini from
the GITEA__storage__MINIO_* envs in the init-app-ini INITCONTAINER. An
initContainer runs once per POD, so restarts re-read the stale file and never
re-render it. The chart's checksum/config pod annotation hashes only the inline
config secret, not the secretKeyRef'd envs, so the 2026-08-02 rotation of
forgejo/forgejo-backup-armor was invisible to it. Nothing is wrong with the
credential or with ARMOR's authz -- only this pod is stale.

[migrated notes from bf-3tglb]
No code change: the acceptance criteria are already met by the current structure, and re-inlining the literal if-let regresses tested behaviour.

Where the Some-Some match lives now: src/governor.rs:1507 window_deltas_from_snapshots matches (Some(prev), Some(curr)) and computes prev_pct/curr_pct + calculate_window_pct_delta entirely inside that arm; the catch-all _ => (None, None, None) computes nothing (verified previously by bf-1z5eg). run_governor_cycle reaches it at src/governor.rs:5172 via compute_and_log_window_deltas, which both cycle paths now share (the de-duplication bf-1uqqx recommended). So delta computation IS only inside a Some-Some block -- factored into a helper rather than open-coded at the call site.

Tried the literal form anyway to test the premise:
    if let (Some(prev), Some(curr)) = (&state.previous_api_snapshot, &state.current_api_snapshot) { ... }
with compute + the three assignments moved inside. It compiles clean (cargo check --all-targets, borrowck fine), but it regresses two things:

2. It drops the documented invariant at src/governor.rs:5177 -- the assignments are unconditional so a stale Some(..) from the previous cycle cannot survive into an interval it does not describe. Inside the if-let, a poll with no baseline leaves last cycle's deltas in state.

Reverted. cargo test --test delta_logging_runtime_test --test governor_cycle_snapshot_test: 10 passed, 0 failed.

Project future capacity utilization under configurable worker scenarios.

### What to Implement
- New `src/simulator.rs` module:
  - `simulate(config: SimConfig) -> Trajectory`:

### Acceptance Criteria

- Read-only — no side effects

issue.description:
## Problem

As of 2026-04-23, every single one of the 50 most recently closed beads in claude-governor is a `docs-*` bead that was auto-created from an alert (`sonnet_cutoff_risk`, `cutoff_imminent`, `emergency_brake_activated`, `collector_offline`) and closed with a commit of the form:

```
Document docs-jnvh as emergency_brake_activated false positive (98% util, -17.2h margin)
Document docs-q4sj as sonnet_cutoff_risk false positive (86% util, -16.2h margin)
Document docs-tggx as cutoff_imminent false positive (99% util, -16.2h margin)
```

**FP rate in the observed window: 50/50 = 100%.** This loop produces ~298 commits/7d — about 25% of total repo-wide commit volume — with zero engineering value.

## Fleet impact

- Workers spend ~25% of capacity round-tripping these alerts (alert fires → `docs-*` bead spawns → worker claims → "document as false positive" commit → close).
- When a worker dies mid-alert-handling, the `docs-*` bead becomes an in_progress zombie. 19 of the 53 total in_progress beads on 2026-04-22 were stuck claude-governor alerts with ages 50h–220h.
- Velocity metrics are inflated: real engineering work is ~127 commits/day vs. a reported ~169. The 500 commits/day target is 25% of the way there, not 34%.

## Suspected root cause

The alert bodies report utilization `81%–99%` alongside margins of `-15.2h` to `-23.2h` (negative). A negative margin at sub-100% util is self-contradictory — either the margin math is wrong or the thresholds are inverted. Whichever it is, the predicate that fires these alerts is broken across every alert type uniformly, not just one.

Starting points for investigation:
- Burn-rate / margin calculation that feeds `sonnet_cutoff_risk`, `cutoff_imminent`, `emergency_brake_activated`.
- The `safe_worker_count` fallback logic (separately tracked in recent `docs-yk3r`, `docs-3gh2`, `docs-khar`, `docs-2dy4` beads — all flagged as bugs, none yet fixed).

## Fix in two parts

**(1) Correct the alert predicates** so the FP rate drops below 5% measured across any 100-bead window.

**(2) Interim mitigation: gate the alert→bead pipeline.** Until (1) lands, stop auto-creating beads for these alert classes. Keep the alert logs for diagnosis; don't burn fleet cycles documenting false positives. Concrete options:
  - Feature flag `governor.alerts.auto_bead = false` (fastest).
  - Require N consecutive cycles in alert state before spawning a bead (smooths out momentary spikes).
  - Suppress spawning when margin and utilization are inconsistent (e.g. negative margin at util < 100%).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] FP rate for `sonnet_cutoff_risk`, `cutoff_imminent`, `emergency_brake_activated`, `collector_offline` measured at <5% over a 100-bead rolling window.
- [ ] Beads are no longer auto-spawned for these alert classes until the FP rate target is met (interim mitigation in place within this bead).
- [ ] Telemetry/dashboard exposes alert FP rate so regressions are visible.
- [ ] New test: negative-margin-at-sub-100%-util alert is suppressed at source (consistency check).
- [ ] Existing zombie `docs-*` beads (ages >6h) are closed out as part of landing this fix.

## Related

- `needle-mv9t` (2026-04-22): cross-workspace mend gap — would clean up zombies produced by this loop, but doesn't address the root cause.
- `docs-yk3r`, `docs-3gh2`, `docs-khar`, `docs-2dy4`: previously-identified governor bugs that likely share upstream causes.
issue.title: Alert thresholding produces 100% false positives; stop auto-creating beads for unvalidated alerts

issue.notes:
[migrated notes from bf-5q0qv]
NOT MET -- no CNPG backup in ns forgejo can currently reach Completed. Follow-up filed as bf-4neof (P1 bug). Not closing this bead green.

Cluster located: iad-ci (KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig), ns forgejo, cluster forgejo-postgres (1/1 Ready, 'Cluster in healthy state', primary forgejo-postgres-1).

Backup inventory: 832 Backup objects, 831 phase=failed, 1 phase=completed.
- The single completed one is forgejo-postgres-daily-20260806150300 (started 2026-08-06T15:03:06Z, stopped 15:03:20Z). It predates the current cluster config, so it does NOT demonstrate that backups work now.
- Most recent scheduled run forgejo-postgres-daily-20260807120300: phase=failed, error='exit status 3'.
- Manual/test attempts by earlier beads (forgejo-postgres-manual-1786091764, forgejo-postgres-test-manual, status-transition-test) all failed too. I did not create another Backup object, because the failure is deterministic at argument-parse time and 831 identical data points already exist.

Failure reason #1 (current, exit status 3): the Cluster spec carries
  spec.backup.barmanObjectStore.data.additionalCommandArgs: ['--min-chunk-size=5G']
(declarative-config commit d89f8e32) and barman rejects it outright:
  barman-cloud-backup: error: argument --min-chunk-size: '5G' is not a valid size string
Confirmed in-pod against barman.clients.cloud_backup.check_size: '5G' REJECTED, '1024MB'/'5GB'/'2GB'/'5MB' all valid. Every backup since 2026-08-07T04:03Z fails here.

Failure reason #2 (pre-existing, exit status 1, what the 5G arg was trying to fix):
  InvalidPartSize: Part size 4837376 is not a multiple of the block size (65536 bytes). ARMOR's uniform-part-size contract (ADR-005) requires block-aligned parts.

Key new finding -- the pending fix will not work either. declarative-config has an UNCOMMITTED working-tree edit changing 5G to 1024MB (forgejo only; queue-db still 5G committed). Its rationale, like d89f8e32's, assumes 'ADR-005 allows the final part to be short'. I probed ARMOR directly with boto3 multipart uploads from inside forgejo-postgres-1:
  single misaligned part (4837376 B)             -> FAIL InvalidPartSize
  single aligned part (4849664 B = 65536*74)     -> OK
  aligned first part + short final part (1000 B) -> FAIL InvalidPartSize on the FINAL part
  misaligned first + short final                 -> FAIL InvalidPartSize
ARMOR requires EVERY part, including the sole/final part, to be a 65536 multiple. The forgejo DB is 40 MB, so min-chunk-size=1024MB yields exactly one ~40MB part that will not be block-aligned and will still be rejected. Probe objects were deleted; 'leftover objects: []' verified.

BackupFailed events: 'kubectl -n forgejo get events --field-selector reason=BackupFailed' returns 'No resources found' -- but that is because CNPG records the failure on the Backup object's status rather than emitting that event reason here, not because failures stopped. The failures are live and ongoing (hourly).

WAL archiving is healthy and unaffected (barman-cloud-wal-archive does not use multipart upload) -- verified 000000010000004B00000021 archived at 2026-08-07T12:03:41Z.

No files changed in this workspace. The fix belongs in the declarative-config repo (and/or ARMOR), which is a separate repo with another agent's uncommitted work in flight; I did not commit or push on its behalf.

issue.close_reason: Row selection, guards, and apportionment all use the delta-measurement span [prev_snap.taken_at, now] as of ced3dc1; span-boundary and in-span apportionment tests added; 766 tests pass. Commit is local only -- remote push blocked by a 503 from git.ardenone.com.
issue.description:
At the annotation call site (src/governor.rs ~line 5570-5615) the time interval used to select rows does not match the interval the percentage delta was measured over.

Rows are selected by:  t0 = state.last_fleet_aggregate.t0, t1 = state.last_fleet_aggregate.t1  (the COLLECTOR's aggregation window)
Delta is computed from: old_pct = prev_snap (captured at prev_usage_snapshot.taken_at) vs new_pct = state.usage.* (captured at 'now') - the API POLL interval

These two intervals are produced by different clocks/cadences and generally do not coincide. The result is that a delta measured over the poll interval is apportioned onto collector rows from a different span, so p5h/p7d/p7ds values are attributed to the wrong interval - and the <2min elapsed guard is evaluated against the collector window rather than the span the delta actually covers.

Fix: make the row-selection interval and the delta-measurement interval the same span. Prefer selecting the i/f rows whose [t0,t1] falls within [prev_snap.taken_at, now], or otherwise justify and document the mapping in a comment.

Depends on the worker-count fix so both call-site inputs are corrected together.

Acceptance criteria:
- Row-selection interval and delta-measurement interval refer to the same span, or the mapping between them is explicitly documented and justified at the call site
- The elapsed-time guard is evaluated against the span the delta actually covers
- Unit test: rows outside the delta-measurement span are not annotated
- Unit test: rows inside the span receive the apportioned delta
- cargo test passes
issue.notes:
[migrated notes from bf-3p0tb]
Implemented in commit ced3dc1 (src/db.rs + src/governor.rs). Annotation call site now uses [prev_snap.taken_at, now] -- the same span the delta is measured over -- for row selection, the guard chain, and annotate_window_pct_deltas. Collector rows are claimed by t1 so contiguous spans partition rows without double-annotation or boundary loss; rationale documented in a comment at the call site. Range queries switched to julianday() because to_rfc3339() emits variable fractional digits. Tests: annotate_window_pct_deltas_ignores_rows_outside_the_delta_span, ..._apportions_across_every_pass_in_the_span, ..._measures_elapsed_over_the_span, and call-site regression test_annotation_follows_the_delta_span_not_the_collector_window. Full suite: 766 passed, 0 failed. NOT PUSHED: git.ardenone.com returns 503 'no available server' on push; commit is local on main (ahead 15). Needs a push once the remote is back.

issue.description:
get_multiplier_at() and effective_hours_remaining() apply the promotion multiplier globally to all windows, but the Promotion struct has an applies_to field that is never checked. The March 2026 promotion only applies to the five_hour window — the seven_day and seven_day_sonnet windows should always get 1.0x.

Fix: add a window parameter to get_multiplier_at() and effective_hours_remaining() (or create per-window variants). The governor should call these per-window when computing capacity_forecast, passing the window name so only the applies_to windows get the boost.

Current state: applies_to is stored in the JSON but ignored. State stores a single effective_hours_remaining instead of per-window values.
issue.title: Promotion multiplier ignores applies_to — applied globally instead of per-window

issue.close_reason: No bucket-policy source of truth exists and no grant is missing; premise disproven. ARMOR (git.ardenone.com/jedarden/ARMOR) is a bespoke single-bucket S3 gateway whose only authz is Credential.ACLs (config.go:20-30,184-201) checked by CheckACL (auth.go:293-317), called ONLY from server.go:715/904 on object paths. The iad-ci deployment (declarative-config k8s/iad-ci/armor/armor-deployment.yaml + armor-configmap.yaml) sets only ARMOR_AUTH_ACCESS_KEY/_SECRET_KEY, so exactly one credential exists with ACLs: nil = full access to bucket iad-ci. forgejo-backup-armor reads the SAME OpenBao properties (rs-manager/iad-ci/armor AUTH_ACCESS_KEY/SECRET) so it IS that credential. ARMOR has no s3:ListBucket/CreateBucket/GetObject action model at all; HeadBucket/CreateBucket are not ACL-gated. Regression commit: NO -- nearest commits to 2026-08-07T01:43Z (11a227ad, 9868516b) are unrelated, armor dir untouched since 2026-08-06 08:47. Real cause is the 2026-08-02 rotation (379bad72/e29db26d/175cc4d4) where forgejo-postgres was restarted but forgejo-gitea was not, leaving a stale app.ini -- matching bf-1tkap. CNPG failures: NO, not shared -- forgejo-postgres has current creds and fails on ARMOR multipart InvalidPartSize/ADR-005 (c8aefe75, d89f8e32, ARMOR fc6c1a86, notes/bf-1zh.md). No changes applied.
issue.description:
Read-only research in the ardenone-cluster / declarative-config domain. Depends on bf-1tkap having identified the exact denied operation.

Find where the S3/IAM policy for the ARMOR object store is declared: which repo, which path, which resource kind (MinIO policy CR, ARMOR-native policy config, ExternalSecret-fed policy doc, or hand-applied). Identify the policy statement(s) that currently attach to the forgejo-backup-armor credential and show why they permit s3:GetObject/s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::iad-ci/forgejo/* but deny the bucket-level action from bf-1tkap (typically a missing s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::iad-ci, and/or missing s3:CreateBucket).

Also determine whether this changed recently: check git history of that policy file and the ARMOR deployment for a commit near 2026-08-07T01:43Z that would explain the regression, and whether the same missing grant explains the failing CNPG backups (forgejo-postgres-daily-*, forgejo-postgres-test-manual) in ns forgejo.

Acceptance criteria:
- Exact file path(s) + repo named for the policy source of truth.
- The current effective policy for the forgejo-backup-armor credential quoted verbatim.
- The specific missing action(s)/resource(s) named.
- A yes/no answer, with evidence, on whether a recent commit caused the regression and whether CNPG backup failures share the cause.
- No changes applied.
issue.notes:
[migrated notes from bf-385rj]
FINDING: There is NO bucket-policy source of truth, and NO missing grant. The task premise
(an IAM-style policy permitting s3:GetObject/PutObject on iad-ci/forgejo/* while denying a
bucket-level action) cannot be expressed in this system. This corroborates bf-1tkap, which
already DISPROVED the object-vs-bucket asymmetry.

== 1. Policy source of truth (exact paths + repos) ==
ARMOR is a bespoke single-bucket S3 gateway, not MinIO. Authorization is env-var-driven
credential config with an OPTIONAL, UNUSED ACL feature. Not a MinIO policy CR, not an
ExternalSecret-fed policy doc, not hand-applied.

Repo https://git.ardenone.com/jedarden/ARMOR.git (local /home/coding/ARMOR):
  internal/config/config.go:20-30    ACLEntry{Bucket,Prefix}; Credential{AccessKey,SecretKey,ACLs}
  internal/config/config.go:184-201  default credential registered with ACLs: nil
  internal/config/config.go:417-464  loadNamedCredentials, optional ARMOR_AUTH_<NAME>_ACL
  internal/server/auth.go:293-317    CheckACL - the ONLY authorization function
  internal/server/server.go:715,904  the ONLY two CheckACL call sites (object paths only)

Repo https://github.com/jedarden/declarative-config.git (local /home/coding/declarative-config):
  k8s/iad-ci/armor/armor-deployment.yaml     container env, lines ~25-95
  k8s/iad-ci/armor/armor-configmap.yaml      ARMOR_BUCKET: "iad-ci", ARMOR_PREFIX: ""
  k8s/iad-ci/armor/armor-externalsecret.yaml OpenBao rs-manager/iad-ci/armor
  k8s/iad-ci/forgejo/forgejo-backup-externalsecret.yaml  the consumer

== 2. Current effective policy for forgejo-backup-armor, verbatim ==
forgejo-backup-externalsecret.yaml pulls AUTH_ACCESS_KEY / AUTH_SECRET_KEY from OpenBao
rs-manager/iad-ci/armor -- the SAME two properties armor-secrets feeds into ARMOR's own
ARMOR_AUTH_ACCESS_KEY / ARMOR_AUTH_SECRET_KEY. So forgejo-backup-armor IS ARMOR's default
credential. Its effective policy is, verbatim (config.go:193-199):

	// Initialize credentials map with default credential
	cfg.Credentials = make(map[string]*Credential)
	cfg.Credentials[cfg.AuthAccessKey] = &Credential{
		AccessKey: cfg.AuthAccessKey,
		SecretKey: cfg.AuthSecretKey,
		ACLs:      nil, // nil means full access to configured bucket
	}

and enforcement, verbatim (auth.go:293-298):

	// CheckACL verifies that the credential is allowed to access the given bucket and key.
	// If the credential has no ACLs (nil), it has full access.
	func CheckACL(cred *config.Credential, bucket, key string) error {
		// No ACLs means full access
		if len(cred.ACLs) == 0 {
			return nil
		}

The iad-ci deployment env sets NO ARMOR_AUTH_<NAME>_ACCESS_KEY, so loadNamedCredentials
finds zero names; cfg.Credentials has exactly one entry, ACLs nil => unconditional full access.

== 3. Missing action(s)/resource(s): NONE ==
ARMOR has no action-level authorization. CheckACL takes only (bucket, key) -- there is no
concept of s3:ListBucket / s3:CreateBucket / s3:GetObject as distinct grants. HeadBucket and
CreateBucket are not ACL-gated at all (CheckACL is called only from server.go:715 and :904,
both object paths). Nothing can be added to a policy because no policy object exists.
The 403 was AUTHENTICATION (SigV4 signature computed over a rotated secret), not authorization
-- exactly as bf-1tkap concluded: the stale key failed EVERY op including GetObject, and the
current key succeeded at HeadBucket/GetObject/PutObject.

== 4. Did a recent commit cause the regression? NO ==
Nearest declarative-config commits to 2026-08-07T01:43Z (= 2026-08-06 21:43 -0400):
  11a227ad 21:40:47 chore(data-stack): take down native-db-writer
  9868516b 21:47:52 feat(polaris): add a read-only data profiler
Neither touches ARMOR auth, forgejo credentials, or any policy.
k8s/iad-ci/armor/ was last touched ~13h earlier and not on credentials:
  68a17a9a 2026-08-06 08:47 fix(iad-ci/armor): disable dead ServiceMonitor/PrometheusRule
  c547d39c 2026-08-06 08:38 fix(iad-ci/armor): mount emptyDir at /tmp
The real causal event is older -- the 2026-08-02 credential rotation:
  379bad72 19:15 chore(iad-ci): force-sync ARMOR auth credential ExternalSecrets
  e29db26d 19:25 chore(iad-ci): restart armor to pick up rotated auth credentials
  175cc4d4 19:27 chore(iad-ci): restart forgejo-postgres to pick up rotated ARMOR backup creds
forgejo-postgres WAS restarted; forgejo-gitea was NOT. The gitea pod dates from ~2026-07-26
(64aa8af4 move to compute1-8, af7a6225 raise memory), matching bf-1tkap's app.ini mtime
2026-07-25. init-app-ini runs only at pod start, so gitea kept the pre-rotation key. The
breakage was LATENT from 2026-08-02 and surfaced whenever gitea next ran storage.Init.

== 5. Do the CNPG backup failures share the cause? NO ==
k8s/iad-ci/forgejo/cnpg-cluster.yaml:60-70 uses the same forgejo-backup-armor secret, but
forgejo-postgres was restarted for the rotation (175cc4d4), so it holds CURRENT credentials.
Its documented failure is ARMOR multipart block-alignment InvalidPartSize (ADR-005), not 403:
  c8aefe75 2026-08-06 08:50 fix(iad-ci): disable base-backup compression to fix ARMOR InvalidPartSize
  d89f8e32 2026-08-06 23:28 fix(iad-ci): ARMOR multipart upload compatibility for CNPG backups
  ARMOR fc6c1a86 2026-08-06 22:51 fix(multipart): allow a lone or final part to be non-block-aligned
  plus the in-file comment block at cnpg-cluster.yaml:71-99 and notes/bf-1zh.md
Different failure mode, different fix. Not a shared cause.

No changes applied (read-only research, as scoped).

issue.description:
## Binding Window Selection and Safe Worker Count

Implement binding window detection across all three windows and safe worker computation.

### Files to Modify
- `src/collector.rs` — add binding window and safe worker logic

### What to Implement
- `pub fn find_binding_window(forecasts: &mut [WindowRecord])`:
  - Find the window with the smallest (most negative) margin_hrs
  - Set `bind = 1` on that window, `bind = 0` on others
  - Compute and set `safe_w` only on the binding window
- `pub fn compute_safe_workers(remaining_pct: f64, hrs_left: f64, p75_rate_per_worker: f64) -> u32`:
  - `safe_w = floor(remaining_pct / (p75_rate_per_worker * hrs_left))`
  - If p75_rate_per_worker is 0 or hrs_left is 0, return u32::MAX (no constraint)
  - Floor to nearest integer (conservative)
- `pub fn compute_window_forecasts(usage_snapshot: &UsageSnapshot, fleet_rates: &FleetRates, config: &Config) -> Vec<WindowRecord>`:
  - Generate 3 WindowRecords (five_hour, seven_day, seven_day_sonnet)
  - Call find_binding_window on the set
  - Return all 3 records ready for JSONL append

### Test Command
```bash
cargo test --lib collector::tests::binding 2>&1; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

### Pass/Fail Criteria
- Unit test: 5h window with margin_hrs=-2 vs 7d with margin_hrs=5 -> 5h is binding
- Unit test: 7d_sonnet most constrained -> it gets bind=1
- Unit test: safe_w computation — remaining=50, hrs_left=10, p75_rate=1.0 -> safe_w=5
- Unit test: safe_w floor behavior — remaining=50, hrs_left=10, p75_rate=1.1 -> safe_w=4 (floor)
- Unit test: safe_w only populated on the binding window, None on others

## Goal
Fire an alert when the fleet's cache-read-to-total-token ratio stays below a configurable threshold for N consecutive polling intervals. This detects workloads that are not benefiting from prompt caching.

## Why
Low cache efficiency means workers are burning more tokens per task than expected. This affects burn rate accuracy and cost. A sustained drop (not just a single spike) indicates a structural issue worth surfacing.

## Implementation
- In alerts.rs: add LowCacheEfficiency alert variant (already has stub per recent commits)
- Track cache_efficiency_ratio per interval in governor state: cache_reads / total_tokens
- If ratio < config.alerts.low_cache_efficiency_threshold (default: 0.3) for >= N consecutive intervals (default: 3): fire alert
- Alert body: current ratio, threshold, consecutive intervals below threshold
- Respect existing per-alert-type cooldown mechanism
- Expose cache_efficiency_ratio in cgov status output
- Add unit tests for threshold boundary, cooldown, recovery

## Config additions (governor.yaml)
alerts:
  low_cache_efficiency_threshold: 0.3
  low_cache_efficiency_consecutive_intervals: 3

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] cache_efficiency_ratio tracked per poll interval
- [ ] Alert fires when ratio sustained below threshold
- [ ] Cooldown respected (no spam)
- [ ] Ratio visible in cgov status --json
- [ ] Unit tests for boundary conditions
issue.title: Add sustained low cache efficiency alert with configurable threshold and window

## Incremental JSONL Reader with Shrinkage Guard

Implement the incremental line reader that seeks to a byte offset and reads new lines, with shrinkage detection for log-rotated files.

### Files to Modify
- `src/collector.rs` — add incremental reader function

### What to Implement
- `pub fn read_new_lines(path: &Path, cursor: &mut CursorStore) -> Result<Vec<String>>`:
  - Get stored offset via cursor.get_offset(path)
  - Check current file size: if file size < stored offset, log warning `[collector] cursor reset for {path} (file shrunk: {stored} -> {actual} bytes)` and reset offset to 0
  - Seek to byte offset, read all bytes to EOF
  - Split into lines, filter out empty lines
  - Update cursor with new byte offset (end of file)
  - Return the new lines as Vec<String>

### Test Command
```bash
cargo test --lib collector::tests::read_new 2>&1; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

### Pass/Fail Criteria
- Unit test: write 3 lines to temp file, read_new_lines with offset 0 returns all 3 lines
- Unit test: incremental read — write 2 lines, read (get 2), write 2 more, read again (get only new 2), verify cursor offset updated
- Unit test: shrinkage guard — write 100 bytes, set cursor offset to 100, truncate file to 10 bytes, read_new_lines resets offset to 0 and returns all content
- Unit test: empty file returns empty Vec
- Unit test: file with trailing newline doesn't produce empty trailing line
- Shrinkage guard must log the warning message (capture log output or use tracing test subscriber)
issue.title: Incremental JSONL reader with shrinkage guard

Probe completed successfully. CRITICAL FINDING: ARMOR's multipart upload implementation appears fundamentally broken, not just enforcing alignment.

- 6/6 multipart upload tests FAILED with InternalError(InvalidPart)
- 1/1 PutObject test PASSED (confirms credentials work)
- NO InvalidPartSize errors detected - ARMOR is NOT enforcing 65536-byte alignment
- All parts fail at CompleteMultipartUpload: 'One or more of the specified parts could not be found'

NEW HYPOTHESIS: ARMOR has a fundamental multipart upload bug preventing ANY completion

issue.description:
## Task: Main Governor Daemon Loop

Implement the core daemon loop that ties together all components into a continuous governor cycle.

### What to Implement
- In `src/governor.rs`:
  - `run_daemon(config: &Config)`: Main loop:
    1. `usage = poll_usage()` — call the poller
    2. `schedule = compute_schedule()` — peak/off-peak, effective hours
    3. `burn_rate = compute_burn_rate()` — read from collector DB, update EMA
    4. `target = compute_target_workers(usage, schedule, burn_rate)` — per-agent targets
    5. `current = count_workers()` — heartbeat + tmux verification
    6. `apply_scaling(current, target)` — scale up/down with hysteresis
    7. `check_alerts(usage, schedule)` — alert conditions
    8. `write_state()` — atomic state file update
    9. `sleep(LOOP_INTERVAL)` — configurable, default 300s
  - Signal handling: SIGINT/SIGTERM -> graceful shutdown (finish current cycle, exit)
  - Error handling: never crash — log errors, continue to next cycle
  - Logging: structured per-cycle summary with window status, worker counts, actions taken
  - `--dry-run` mode: compute and log everything but skip apply_scaling()

### Files
- `src/governor.rs` (extend)
- `src/main.rs` (add `cgov daemon` and `cgov daemon --dry-run` subcommands)

### Testing Requirements
- Integration test: mock all components, verify correct call sequence
- Unit test: error in one component doesn't crash daemon (logs and continues)
- Unit test: dry-run mode logs target but doesn't scale
- Unit test: signal handling triggers clean exit
- Unit test: state file updated after each cycle

### Acceptance Criteria
- Daemon runs continuously until interrupted
- Never crashes on component errors
- dry-run mode fully functional
- Structured logging per cycle
- State file atomically updated each cycle
- Graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P4 worker manager (docs-x8d) — needs scale_up/scale_down
- Depends on: P4 target computation (docs-9uz) — needs compute_target_workers

Fixed false positive sonnet_cutoff_risk alert

The alert was firing even when margin_hrs was positive (safe). This was caused by missing validation of the margin_hrs field in the alert condition.

Per burn_rate.rs formula:
- margin_hrs = predicted_exhaustion_hours - hours_remaining
- Positive margin_hrs = safe (exhaustion after reset)
- Negative margin_hrs = risky (exhaustion before reset)

The fix adds a check for margin_hrs < 0.0 in both sonnet_cutoff_risk and session_cutoff_risk alert functions to prevent false positives from corrupted state or sign convention mismatches between modules.

Fix commit: 26c399d
Regression tests added to prevent recurrence.

Repo-side dedup was already done by 504da60; the remaining gap was that existing installs still carried a stale cgov.service. cgov init/enable/disable --purge now stop, disable, and delete it before daemon-reload (3 tests). issue.description: config/cgov.service and config/claude-governor.service both ship as 'the governor daemon' unit for the same logical process, but they differ in ways that matter: claude-governor.service runs 'cgov _daemon' (the hidden systemd-oriented subcommand, Restart=always, Wants=claude-token-collector.service) while cgov.service runs 'cgov daemon' (the public foreground subcommand meant for manual/interactive use, Restart=on-failure, no Wants dependency). An operator who installs/enables cgov.service instead of claude-governor.service gets different restart semantics and no ordering guarantee relative to the token collector, with no clear signal which one is canonical. docs/plan/plan.md's File Layout section documents cgov.service as 'Systemd user service — governor daemon' and claude-governor.service as 'Alternative governor daemon service name', which is itself the source of the ambiguity. Pick one canonical unit name and ExecStart target (claude-governor.service invoking the hidden _daemon subcommand is the correct one, matching Phase 6.2 of the plan), remove or clearly deprecate the other in config/, install.sh, and cgov init/enable, and update the plan's File Layout section to stop presenting them as equally valid alternatives. On this host both units currently exist under ~/.config/systemd/user/ and are both disabled, so this is a good time to also clean up the live install once the fix lands.

Committed locally as 4fcc9ea. PUSH BLOCKED: git.ardenone.com returns 503 'no available server' on every attempt (7 tries over ~3min). Pre-existing outage — main was already 22 commits ahead of origin before this commit; now 23. Commit needs pushing once the remote is back.

Findings: config/cgov.service was already deleted from the repo by 504da60 (bead bf-4vf4q), and src/ referenced only claude-governor.service. install.sh installs no units at all (it just prints 'cgov enable'). plan.md's File Layout no longer listed cgov.service as an 'Alternative governor daemon service name'. So the repo-side dedup described in the bead was largely already done.

The real remaining gap: deleting the source file does not converge hosts that installed before it. This host still had ~/.config/systemd/user/cgov.service (dated Mar 21, ExecStart=cgov daemon, Restart=on-failure, no Wants= on the collector), disabled but enable-able by name. issue.description:
## Goal
Replace the current binding window selection (based solely on margin_hrs) with a composite risk score that weights each window by:
- **Margin** (hours remaining before exhaustion)
- **Duration** (5h window is higher risk than 7d window at same margin%)
- **Volatility** (p25/p50/p75 cone spread — wide cone = uncertain forecast = higher risk)
- **Time-to-reset** (how soon can we recover if we exhaust?)

## Why
The current approach picks the window with the smallest margin_hrs absolute. But a 5-hour window with 1hr margin is far more dangerous than a 7-day window with 6hr margin. Duration and volatility should amplify the risk score.

## Proposed Formula
risk_score = (1.0 - margin_pct) * duration_weight * volatility_factor
- duration_weight: 5h → 3.0, 7d → 1.0, 7d-sonnet → 1.5
- volatility_factor: cone_ratio (p75 - p25) / p50 — wider = higher risk

## Implementation
- Add risk_score computation in burn_rate.rs per-window
- Update binding window selection in governor.rs to use max risk_score
- Surface risk_score in state.rs and status_display.rs
- Add unit tests for composite risk edge cases

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] risk_score computed for each window
- [ ] Binding window selected by max risk_score (not min margin_hrs)
- [ ] risk_score visible in cgov status --json
- [ ] Unit tests pass
issue.title: Composite risk optimization: weight binding window by duration, volatility, and margin

Validate declared promotion multipliers by comparing peak vs off-peak consumption ratios.

### What to Implement
- In `src/schedule.rs` or `src/burn_rate.rs`:

  - Validation rules:
    - If observed_ratio within 10% of declared multiplier: validated=true
    - If observed_ratio < 1.2: promotion likely not applying, fall back to 1x, log warning
    - If observed_ratio > 2.5: unexpected, log anomaly, use observed ratio

## Task: Forecast Confidence Cone

Replace single-point exhaustion predictions with range estimates using per-worker variance.

### What to Implement
- In `src/burn_rate.rs` (extend):
  - Compute per-window exhaustion prediction cone:
    - rate_p25 = ema_rate - 0.675 * stddev (optimistic, 25th percentile)
    - rate_p50 = ema_rate (expected)
    - rate_p75 = ema_rate + 0.675 * stddev (conservative, 75th percentile)
    - exh_hrs_p25 = remaining_pct / (rate_p25 * workers) — best case
    - exh_hrs_p50 = remaining_pct / (rate_p50 * workers) — expected
    - exh_hrs_p75 = remaining_pct / (rate_p75 * workers) — worst case
  - `cone_ratio = exh_hrs_p25 / exh_hrs_p75` (or p75/p25 of rates)
  - Decision logic modulation:
    - Narrow cone (ratio < 1.5): act on p50 (confident)
    - Wide cone (ratio > 2.0): act on p75 (conservative)
    - Between: linear blend between p50 and p75
  - Extend `w` record fields: `exh_hrs_p25`, `exh_hrs_p50`, `exh_hrs_p75`, `cone_ratio`
  - Extend `cgov status` output: `CUTOFF 2.0-3.8h` range instead of single value
  - Extend `cgov simulate` to output three trajectory lines (best/expected/worst)
  - Safe mode interaction: always use p75 regardless of cone width

### Files
- `src/burn_rate.rs` (extend)
- `src/collector.rs` (extend w record)
- `src/cli.rs` (extend status display)

### Acceptance Criteria

## Task: Instance (i) and Fleet (f) JSONL Record Writer

Implement the JSONL record generation for instance-level and fleet-level token consumption data.

### What to Implement
- In `src/collector.rs`:
  - `InstanceRecord` struct matching the wide `i` record schema:
    - `r: "i"`, `ts`, `t0`, `t1`, `sess`, `sid`, `model`, `pk` (peak flag), `hr_et`, `dow`
    - Token columns: `input-n`, `input-usd`, `output-n`, `output-usd`, `r-cache-n`, `r-cache-usd`, `w-cache-n`, `w-cache-usd`, `w-cache-1h-n`, `w-cache-1h-usd`, `total-usd`
    - Window pct fields: `p5h`, `p7d`, `p7ds` (null at write time, annotated later by governor)
  - `FleetRecord` struct matching the wide `f` record schema:
    - `r: "f"`, timestamps, `pk`, `hr_et`, `dow`, `workers`
    - Per-model columns: `{model}-{tok_type}-n`, `{model}-{tok_type}-usd` for all configured models
    - Fleet totals: `total-usd`, `p75-usd-hr`, `std-usd-hr`
    - Window snapshots: `p5h`, `p7d`, `p7ds`, `usd-per-pct-7ds`
  - `aggregate_to_fleet(instances: &[InstanceRecord]) -> FleetRecord`: Sum instance records, compute per-worker stats (mean, p75, stddev)
  - `append_jsonl(path: &Path, records: &[serde_json::Value])`: Atomic append to JSONL file
  - Peak/off-peak detection: `is_peak(t: DateTime) -> bool` — peak = 8AM-2PM ET weekdays
  - `hr_et` and `dow` computation from timestamp

### Files
- `src/collector.rs`

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: single instance record serializes correctly to expected JSON shape
- Unit test: fleet record aggregation from 2 instances — verify sums and per-worker stats
- Unit test: p75 and stddev computation with 3+ synthetic instances
- Unit test: peak flag correctly set for various times (weekday 10am=peak, weekday 3pm=off-peak, weekend=off-peak)
- Unit test: JSONL append atomicity (no partial writes)
- Unit test: zero-activity models produce zero-filled columns in fleet record

### Acceptance Criteria
- Records match the exact JSONL schema from the plan (field names, types)
- Fleet record includes all configured models even when inactive (zero-filled)
- Per-worker variance stats computed correctly
- JSONL file grows append-only, one JSON object per line

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P1b dollar computation (docs-o6d) — needs DollarBreakdown
- Depends on: P1b usage block parser (docs-s7l) — needs UsageRecord

## Task: Per-Instance Burn Rate Computation

Compute per-instance dollar_burn and pct_burn from token collector records.

### What to Implement
- New `src/burn_rate.rs` module:
  - `InstanceBurnRate` struct: session, model, window, dollar_per_hour, pct_per_hour, elapsed_hours
  - `compute_instance_burn(record: &InstanceRecord, elapsed_hours: f64) -> Vec<InstanceBurnRate>`:
    - For each window with non-null pct_delta: `pct_per_hour = pct_delta / elapsed_hours`
    - `dollar_per_hour = total_usd / elapsed_hours`
  - Read latest complete interval `i` records from token-history.db
  - Guard conditions:
    - Skip if elapsed < 2 minutes (too short)
    - Skip if pct_delta is null (not yet annotated)
    - Skip if all pct_deltas are 0 but tokens > 0 (API rounding artifact)
  - Window reset detection: if `current_utilization < previous_utilization - 1.0`, discard that interval for that window

### Files
- `src/burn_rate.rs` (new module)
- `src/main.rs` (add `mod burn_rate`)

### Testing Requirements

- Unit test: guard — skip interval < 2 minutes
- Unit test: guard — skip null pct_delta
- Unit test: guard — skip zero pct_delta with non-zero tokens
- Unit test: window reset detection (utilization drop > 1%)
- Unit test: multi-window burn (each window computed independently)

### Acceptance Criteria

- All guard conditions enforced
- Window reset mid-interval correctly discards affected window only

Implemented in commit 74dd4de: alert dedup is now a stateful per-episode lifecycle instead of a cooldown timer. An episode is one continuous stretch during which a condition holds, keyed by alert type + scope. First cycle true -> create ONE bead and store its id in governor-state.json under open_alert_beads; while it stays true -> no new bead, refresh the existing one's notes at most once per cooldown_minutes; first cycle not true -> auto-close the bead with a reason and drop the entry. cooldown_minutes survives only as an anti-flap floor on OPENING a new episode after one resolves, so a flapping condition still cannot mint a bead per toggle. Bead volume is now bounded by distinct incidents rather than elapsed time -- the structural cause of the 226 sonnet_cutoff_risk / 160 cutoff_imminent bead pileup.

Fixed false positive sonnet_cutoff_risk alert

The alert was firing even when margin_hrs was positive (safe). This was caused by missing validation of the margin_hrs field in the alert condition.

Per burn_rate.rs formula:
- margin_hrs = predicted_exhaustion_hours - hours_remaining
- Positive margin_hrs = safe (exhaustion after reset)
- Negative margin_hrs = risky (exhaustion before reset)

The fix adds a check for margin_hrs < 0.0 in both sonnet_cutoff_risk and session_cutoff_risk alert functions to prevent false positives from corrupted state or sign convention mismatches between modules.
